title.zh: 卷277 列傳六十四 于成龙 彭鹏 陈瑸 陈鹏年 施世纶
title.en: Volume 277 Biographies 64: Yu Chenglong, Peng Peng, Chen Bin, Chen Pengnian, Shi Shilun
title.raw: 卷277 列傳六十四 于成龙 彭鹏 陈瑸 陈鹏年 施世纶

sentences.zh: 列傳六十四

translations.literal: Biographies 64
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 64

sentences.zh: -{于}-成龍孫準彭鵬陳瑸陳鵬年施世綸

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong, Sun Zhun, Peng Peng, Chen Bin, Chen Pengnian, and Shi Shilun
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong, Sun Zhun, Peng Peng, Chen Bin, Chen Pengnian, and Shi Shilun

sentences.zh: -{于}-成龍，字北溟，山西永寧人。

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong, whose courtesy name was Beiming, was a native of Yongning in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong, styled Beiming, came from Yongning in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎間副榜貢生。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign of the Ming he was a tribute student on the secondary list.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he had passed the provincial examination as a secondary-list graduate during the Chongzhen era.

sentences.zh: 順治十八年，謁選，授廣西羅城知縣，年四十五矣。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shunzhi he presented himself for appointment and was made magistrate of Luocheng in Guangxi, at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 he went up for selection and received appointment as magistrate of Luocheng in Guangxi—he was forty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 羅城居萬山中，盛瘴癘，瑤、僮獷悍，初隸版籍。

translations.literal: Luocheng lay deep among ten thousand mountains, rife with miasma; the Yao and Zhuang were fierce and unruly and had only lately been brought under the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Luocheng sat buried in rugged mountains where pestilence flourished; the Yao and Zhuang were wild and defiant, having only recently been entered on the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 方兵後，遍地榛莽，縣中居民僅六家，無城郭廨舍。

translations.literal: Just after the wars the land was everywhere overgrown with scrub; within the county there were only six households, and there were neither walls nor government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from the wars, the district was choked with wilderness; only six families remained in the county seat, with no city walls or yamen buildings at all.

sentences.zh: 成龍到官，召吏民拊循之，申明保甲。

translations.literal: When Chenglong took office he summoned clerks and people to comfort and guide them, and made clear the baojia system.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Chenglong gathered officials and commoners to reassure them and set the mutual-responsibility baojia system in order.

sentences.zh: 盜發即時捕治，請於上官，讞實即處決，民安其居。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits appeared he captured and punished them at once; he reported to his superiors, and once guilt was verified he executed them, so the people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The moment banditry broke out he seized and punished the culprits, sought approval from above, and executed those whose guilt was proved—so the people could live without fear.

sentences.zh: 鄰瑤歲來殺掠，成龍集鄉兵將搗其巢，瑤懼，誓不敢犯羅山境。

translations.literal: Neighboring Yao came each year to kill and plunder; Chenglong gathered militia to storm their lairs, and the Yao, in fear, swore never again to violate the borders of Luoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Each year neighboring Yao raided and slaughtered; Chenglong mustered local militia to strike their strongholds, and the Yao, terrified, vowed never again to cross into Luocheng territory.

sentences.zh: 民益得盡力耕耘。

translations.literal: The people were all the more able to devote themselves fully to cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: The people could at last farm in peace and give their fields their full attention.

sentences.zh: 居羅山七年，與民相愛如家人父子。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Luoshan seven years, and he and the people loved one another like members of one family, father and sons.
translations.idiomatic: He spent seven years in Luocheng, and he and the people cherished one another like kin—father and sons under one roof.

sentences.zh: 牒上官請寬徭役，疏鹺引，建學宮，創設養濟院，凡所當興罷​​者，次第舉行，縣大治。

translations.literal: He memorialized his superiors to lighten corvée, to open salt routes, to build a school, and to establish a poor-relief hospice; whatever ought to be undertaken or abolished he carried out in turn, and the county was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned above to ease labor levies, open salt transport routes, erect a school, and found a relief hospice for the destitute; project by project he carried through every reform the county needed, until Luocheng was thoroughly well ordered.

sentences.zh: 總督盧興祖等薦卓異。

translations.literal: The governor-general Lu Xingzu and others recommended him as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lu Xingzu and others nominated him for outstanding merit.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，遷四川合州知州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he was transferred to be prefect of Hezhou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he was moved to serve as prefect of Hezhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四川大亂後，州中遺民裁百餘，正賦僅十五兩，而供役繁重。

translations.literal: After the great disorder in Sichuan the surviving people in the prefecture amounted to little more than a hundred; regular land tax was only fifteen taels, yet the burden of supply duties was heavy.
translations.idiomatic: After Sichuan's great upheaval barely a hundred people remained in the prefecture; regular tax revenue stood at only fifteen taels, while supply and corvée obligations weighed crushingly on them.

sentences.zh: 成龍請革宿弊，招民墾田，貸以牛種，期月戶增至千。

translations.literal: Chenglong requested the abolition of long-standing abuses, summoned people to open fields, and lent them oxen and seed; within a month households increased to a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong petitioned to sweep away entrenched abuses, drew settlers to reclaim farmland, and lent them oxen and seed grain; within a month household registers swelled to a thousand.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣黃岡同知，駐岐亭。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be sub-prefect of Huanggang in Huguang, stationed at Qiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to sub-prefect of Huanggang in Huguang and posted at Qiting.

sentences.zh: 岐亭故多盜，白晝行劫，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Qiting had long been full of bandits who robbed in broad daylight, and no one dared challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiting had always been notorious for brigands who plundered in daylight while no one dared stand against them.

sentences.zh: 成龍撫其渠彭百齡，貰罪，令捕盜自贖。

translations.literal: Chenglong won over their leader Peng Bailing, remitted his punishment, and ordered him to capture bandits to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong won over their ringleader Peng Bailing, pardoned his crimes, and charged him to hunt down bandits as his path to redemption.

sentences.zh: 嘗察知盜所在，偽為丐者，入其巢，與雜處十餘日，盡得其平時行劫狀。

translations.literal: Once, having learned where the bandits were, he disguised himself as a beggar, entered their den, and mingled with them for more than ten days, learning in full their usual manner of robbery.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, having traced the bandits' hideout, he disguised himself as a mendicant, slipped into their lair, and lived among them for ten-odd days until he knew every detail of their raids.

sentences.zh: 乃出呼役械諸盜，具獄辭，駢縛坑之，他盜皆遠竄。

translations.literal: Then he came forth, called his runners to seize the bandits with weapons, drew up the case records, bound them in pairs and buried them in a pit, and the other bandits all fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: He then emerged, summoned his constables to seize the gang, drew up the indictments, bound them in pairs and buried them in a mass grave—and the rest of the brigands scattered to distant parts.

sentences.zh: 嘗微行村堡，周訪閭里情偽，遇盜及他疑獄，輒踪跡得之，民驚服。

translations.literal: He would travel in disguise through villages and forts, making the rounds to learn the truth of neighborhood affairs; whenever he met bandits or other doubtful cases he would trace them and obtain them, and the people were astonished and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He often went about in plain dress through villages and stockades, sounding out local conditions; bandits and puzzling cases alike he tracked to their source, to the people's awe and admiration.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張朝珍舉卓異。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Zhang Chaozhen recommended him as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Zhang Chaozhen nominated him for outstanding service.

sentences.zh: 十三年，署武昌知府。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he served as acting prefect of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he acted as prefect of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂犯湖南，師方攻岳州，檄成龍造浮橋濟師，甫成，山水發，橋圮，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui invaded Hunan; the army was then attacking Yuezhou, and Chenglong was ordered to build a pontoon bridge to ferry the troops; it was barely finished when mountain floods rose and the bridge collapsed, and he was stripped of office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui struck Hunan and imperial forces were besieging Yuezhou, Chenglong was ordered to throw a pontoon bridge across the river for the army; scarcely was it finished when floods swept it away, and he lost his post as punishment.

sentences.zh: 三桂散偽劄遍湖北州縣，麻城、大冶、黃岡、黃安諸盜，皆倚山結寨應三桂。

translations.literal: Sangui scattered forged commissions throughout the prefectures and counties of Hubei; bandits of Macheng, Daye, Huanggang, Huang'an, and elsewhere all leaned on the mountains to build stockades in response to Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui spread forged commissions across Hubei; brigands in Macheng, Daye, Huanggang, Huang'an, and neighboring districts all fortified mountain strongholds in his cause.

sentences.zh: 妖人黃金龍匿興寧山中，謀內亂。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Huang Jinlong hid in the mountains of Xingning and plotted internal rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Huang Jinlong lay hidden in the Xingning hills, plotting an uprising from within.

sentences.zh: 劉君孚者，嘗為成龍役，善捕盜，亦得三桂劄，與金龍等結大盜周鐵爪，據曹家河以叛。

translations.literal: Liu Junfu had once served under Chenglong and was skilled at capturing bandits; he too received a commission from Sangui, joined with Jinlong and the great bandit Zhou Tiezhua, seized Caojia River, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Junfu, who had once worked for Chenglong and excelled at hunting bandits, also received a commission from Sangui; he allied with Jinlong and the notorious Zhou Tiezhua, seized Caojia River, and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 朝珍以成龍舊治得民心，檄往招撫。

translations.literal: Chaozhen, because Chenglong's former rule had won the people's hearts, ordered him to go and offer pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhen, knowing Chenglong still commanded the people's loyalty from his earlier tenure, dispatched him to win the rebels over by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 成龍诇知君孚雖反，眾未合，猶豫持兩端。

translations.literal: Chenglong learned by inquiry that although Junfu had rebelled, his followers were not yet united and he still hesitated between two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong's scouts reported that though Junfu had turned rebel, his forces were not yet consolidated and he still wavered between loyalty and defiance.

sentences.zh: 兼程趨賊砦，距十里許止宿，榜示自首者免罪，來者日千計，皆貸之。

translations.literal: He pressed on day and night toward the bandit stockade, halted to lodge when still about ten li away, and posted a notice that those who surrendered themselves would be spared punishment; those who came numbered thousands each day, and he pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He marched day and night toward the rebel camp, halted ten li short, and posted notice that self-surrender meant amnesty; thousands came each day, and he spared them all.

sentences.zh: 先遣鄉約諭君孚，降者待以不死。

translations.literal: He first sent the village covenant elders to instruct Junfu that those who submitted would be treated with the promise of life.
translations.idiomatic: First he sent village elders to tell Junfu that surrender would spare his life.

sentences.zh: 乃策黑騾往，從者二，張蓋鳴鉦，迳入賊舍。

translations.literal: Then he mounted a black mule and went, with only two attendants, raising an umbrella and sounding gongs, and went straight into the bandits' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then he rode a black mule with only two followers, canopy raised and gongs sounding, straight into the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 呼君孚出見，叩頭受撫，降其眾數千，分立區保，籍其勇力者，督令進討。

translations.literal: He called Junfu out to meet him; Junfu kowtowed and accepted pacification; he reduced several thousand of their followers, set up separate district baojia units, registered the strong among them, and supervised them in advancing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Junfu forth; Junfu kowtowed and submitted, and Chenglong disbanded several thousand followers into local baojia units, enrolled the able-bodied, and set them to pursue the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 金龍走紙棚河，與其渠鄒君申往保山砦，成龍擒斬之。

translations.literal: Jinlong fled to Zhipeng River; with his lieutenant Zou Junshen he went to Baoshan stockade, and Chenglong captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlong fled toward Zhipeng River and, with his lieutenant Zou Junshen, made for Baoshan stockade; Chenglong seized and executed them both.

sentences.zh: 朝珍以聞，請復官，即擢黃州知府，上允之。

translations.literal: Chaozhen reported this and requested restoration of his office; he was at once promoted to prefect of Huangzhou, and the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhen reported the success and petitioned for Chenglong's reinstatement; the court immediately promoted him to prefect of Huangzhou, which the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 諸盜何士榮反永寧鄉，陳鼎業反陽邏，劉啟業反石陂，周鐵爪、鮑世庸反泉畈，各有眾數千，號東山賊，遙與湖口、寧州諸盜合，將趨黃州。

translations.literal: Among the bandits He Shirong rebelled at Yongning township, Chen Dingye at Yangluo, Liu Qiye at Shipi, Zhou Tiezhua and Bao Shiyong at Quanfan; each had followers numbering in the thousands, and they were called the Eastern Mountain bandits; from afar they joined with bandits of Hukou, Ningzhou, and elsewhere, and were about to march on Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Shirong rose at Yongning township, Chen Dingye at Yangluo, Liu Qiye at Shipi, and Zhou Tiezhua with Bao Shiyong at Quanfan—each commanding thousands and known collectively as the Eastern Mountain rebels. In concert with brigands from Hukou and Ningzhou they were converging on Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時諸鎮兵皆從師徇湖南，州中吏民裁數百，議退保麻城。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison troops of the various commands had all followed the army to campaign in Hunan; officials and people in the prefecture amounted to only a few hundred, and there was talk of falling back to defend Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: All regional garrisons had marched south with the Hunan campaign; barely a few hundred officials and civilians remained in the prefecture, and some urged retreat to the safety of Macheng.

sentences.zh: 成龍曰：「黃州，七郡門戶，我師屯荊、岳，轉運取道於此。

translations.literal: Chenglong said: "Huangzhou is the gateway of seven prefectures; our army is encamped at Jing and Yue, and transport takes its route through here.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong said, "Huangzhou is the gateway to seven prefectures. Our armies hold Jingzhou and Yuezhou, and all supply lines run through here.

sentences.zh: 棄此不守，荊、岳且瓦解。」

translations.literal: If we abandon this place and do not defend it, Jing and Yue will soon collapse."
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon it, the Jing-Yue front will unravel.

sentences.zh: 誓死不去。

translations.literal: He swore he would die rather than leave.
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to hold the city or die in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 遂集鄉勇得二千人，遣黃岡知縣李經政攻陽邏，得鼎業誅之。

translations.literal: He then gathered militia to the number of two thousand, sent the Huanggang magistrate Li Jingzheng to attack Yangluo, captured Dingye, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered two thousand local militia and sent Huanggang Magistrate Li Jingzheng against Yangluo; Dingye was captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 士榮率賊數犯，自牧馬崖分兩路來犯。

translations.literal: Shirong led the bandits in repeated attacks, dividing into two columns from Muma Cliff to assail them.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong led repeated rebel assaults, splitting his force at Muma Cliff to attack along two routes.

sentences.zh: 成龍遣千總羅登雲以千人當東路，而自當西路。

translations.literal: Chenglong sent the battalion commander Luo Dengyun with a thousand men to hold the eastern route, while he himself faced the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong sent Battalion Commander Luo Dengyun with a thousand men to hold the eastern approach while he took the western line himself.

sentences.zh: 令千總吳之蘭攻左，武舉張尚聖攻右，成龍力衝其中堅。

translations.literal: He ordered the battalion commander Wu Zhilan to attack on the left, the military licentiate Zhang Shangsheng on the right, and Chenglong himself charged the enemy center with force.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Battalion Commander Wu Zhilan against the left flank, military licentiate Zhang Shangsheng against the right, and drove personally into the enemy center.

sentences.zh: 戰合，之蘭中槍死，師少卻；

translations.literal: When battle joined, Zhilan was struck by a musket ball and died, and the army fell back somewhat;
translations.idiomatic: As the fight joined, Zhilan was shot dead and the line wavered;

sentences.zh: 成龍策馬冒矢石迳前，顧千總李茂升曰：「我死，汝歸報巡撫！」

translations.literal: Chenglong spurred his horse through arrows and stones straight forward, turned to the battalion commander Li Maosheng and said: "If I die, you return and report to the governor!"
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong spurred through a hail of arrows and stones, turned to Battalion Commander Li Maosheng, and cried, "If I fall, you ride back and tell the governor!"

sentences.zh: 茂升戰甚力，尚聖自右出賊後，賊大敗，生致士榮，檻送朝珍，遂進克泉畈。

translations.literal: Maosheng fought with great force; Shangsheng came out on the right behind the bandits; the bandits were utterly defeated; Shirong was captured alive and sent in a caged cart to Chaozhen; then they advanced and took Quanfan.
translations.idiomatic: Maosheng fought ferociously; Shangsheng swung around the rebel right and struck from behind. The enemy broke completely; Shirong was taken alive and sent in a cage to Chaozhen, and the force went on to capture Quanfan.

sentences.zh: 凡二十四日，東山賊悉平。

translations.literal: Within twenty-four days in all, the Eastern Mountain bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In twenty-four days the Eastern Mountain rebels were wholly suppressed.

sentences.zh: 十五年，歲饉，訛言復起。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year there was famine, and false rumors arose again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year famine struck and alarming rumors spread anew.

sentences.zh: 成龍修治赤壁亭榭，日與僚吏歗詠其中，民心大定。

translations.literal: Chenglong repaired the pavilions at Red Cliff, and each day drank and sang poetry there with his subordinates, and popular sentiment was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong restored the Red Cliff pavilions and spent his days there drinking and composing verse with his staff, until public anxiety subsided entirely.

sentences.zh: 會丁繼母憂，總督蔡毓榮奏請奪情視事。

translations.literal: It happened that he entered mourning for his stepmother; Governor-General Cai Yurong memorialized requesting that he be released from mourning to continue in office.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his stepmother, Governor-General Cai Yurong petitioned the throne to exempt him from leave so he could remain at his post.

sentences.zh: 十六年，增設江防道，駐黃州，即以命成龍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the River Defense circuit was newly established, stationed at Huangzhou, and Chenglong was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year a new River Defense circuit was created at Huangzhou, and Chenglong was placed in command.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to Fujian as provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became Fujian surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功迭犯泉、漳諸郡，民以通海獲罪，株連數千人，獄成，當駢戮。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong repeatedly invaded the prefectures of Quan and Zhang; people were convicted for communicating with the sea, and thousands were implicated by association; when the cases were concluded they were to be executed in batches.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong was raiding Quanzhou and Zhangzhou repeatedly; thousands were implicated for coastal contacts with the enemy, and when trials concluded they faced mass execution.

sentences.zh: 成龍白康親王杰書，言所連引多平民，宜省釋。

translations.literal: Chenglong informed the Prince Kang Jieshu that most of those implicated were common people and ought to be released after review.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong appealed to Prince Kang Jieshu, arguing that most of those caught up in the cases were ordinary civilians who should be released.

sentences.zh: 王素重成龍，悉從其請。

translations.literal: The prince had long valued Chenglong and followed all his requests.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had always held Chenglong in high regard and granted every request.

sentences.zh: 遇疑獄，輒令訊鞫。

translations.literal: Whenever he encountered doubtful cases he would order them interrogated and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a case seemed doubtful he ordered it reinvestigated personally.

sentences.zh: 判決明允，獄無淹滯。

translations.literal: His judgments were clear and fair, and no cases languished in prison.
translations.idiomatic: His judgments were lucid and just, and no prisoner languished in detention.

sentences.zh: 軍中多掠良民子女沒為奴婢，成龍集資贖歸之。

translations.literal: In the army many seized the sons and daughters of good common people and made them slaves; Chenglong raised funds to ransom and return them.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers had seized countless commoners' children as slaves; Chenglong raised funds to buy them back and restore them to their families.

sentences.zh: 巡撫吳興祚疏薦廉能第一，遷布政使。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Wu Xingzuo memorialized recommending him first in integrity and ability, and he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Wu Xingzuo ranked him first in integrity and competence, and he was promoted to administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 師駐福建，月徵莝夫數万，累民，成龍白王罷之。

translations.literal: The army was stationed in Fujian and each month drafted tens of thousands of fodder carriers, burdening the people; Chenglong informed the prince and had this abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With the army encamped in Fujian, tens of thousands of fodder porters were levied monthly, crushing the populace; Chenglong persuaded the prince to end the practice.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢直隸巡撫，蒞任，戒州縣私加火耗餽遺上官。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to provincial governor of Zhili; on taking office he forbade prefectures and counties privately to add meltage fees and present gifts to superiors.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made governor of Zhili; on arrival he forbade counties and prefectures from padding surcharges or showering superiors with gifts.

sentences.zh: 令既行，道府劾州縣，州縣即訐道府不得餽遺挾嫌，疏請嚴定處分，下部議行。

translations.literal: Once the order was in force, circuit and prefectural officials impeached the counties, and the counties in turn accused the circuit and prefectural officials of using the ban on gifts to harbor private grudges; he memorialized requesting strict fixed penalties, and the ministry deliberated and put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order took effect, circuit and prefectural officers denounced county magistrates, who retorted that their superiors were using the gift ban to settle private scores. Chenglong memorialized for fixed penalties, and the ministry approved and enforced them.

sentences.zh: 宣化所屬東西二城與懷安、蔚州二衛舊有水沖沙壓地千八百頃，前政金世德請除糧，未行，為民累；

translations.literal: Within the jurisdiction of Xuanhua, the eastern and western cities together with the two guards of Huai'an and Yuzhou had formerly eighteen hundred qing of land washed away by floods and buried in sand; the previous administration of Jin Shide had requested removal of grain tax, but it had not been carried out, and it remained a burden on the people;
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhua jurisdiction, the eastern and western districts together with Huai'an and Yuzhou guards still owed tax on eighteen hundred qing of land long since washed away or buried in sand; Jin Shide's earlier petition to remit the levy had never been granted, and the burden still crushed the people;

sentences.zh: 成龍复疏請，從之。

translations.literal: Chenglong again memorialized requesting this, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong petitioned again, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 又以其地夏秋屢被災，請治賑。

translations.literal: Moreover, because that region had repeatedly suffered disasters in summer and autumn, he requested relief administration.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region had suffered repeated summer and autumn disasters, he also requested famine relief.

sentences.zh: 別疏劾青縣知縣趙履謙貪墨，論如律。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he impeached the Qing county magistrate Zhao Lüqian for corruption, and he was sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he impeached Qing County Magistrate Zhao Lüqian for graft; the court sentenced him as the law required.

sentences.zh: 二十年，入覲，召對，上褒為「清官第一」，因問剿撫黃州土賊狀，成龍對：「臣惟宣布上威德，未有他能。」

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he came to audience; summoned to converse, the emperor praised him as "the foremost honest official," and asked about the situation in suppressing and pacifying the native bandits of Huangzhou; Chenglong replied: "Your servant has only proclaimed Your Majesty's majesty and virtue; I have had no other ability."
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he attended court and was granted an audience. The emperor hailed him as "the foremost honest official" and asked how he had pacified Huangzhou's mountain rebels. Chenglong answered, "Your servant has done nothing but proclaim Your Majesty's majesty and benevolence—I had no other gift."

sentences.zh: 問：「屬吏中亦有清廉否？」

translations.literal: He asked: "Are there also honest men among your subordinates?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Are any of your subordinates likewise incorrupt?"

sentences.zh: 成龍以知縣謝錫袞，同知何如玉、羅京對。

translations.literal: Chenglong named the magistrate Xie Xiduo, and the sub-prefects He Ruyu and Luo Jing in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong named Magistrate Xie Xiduo and Sub-Prefects He Ruyu and Luo Jing.

sentences.zh: 复諭劾趙履謙甚當，成龍奏：「履謙過而不改，臣不得已劾之。」

translations.literal: The emperor again instructed that his impeachment of Zhao Lüqian was very apt; Chenglong submitted: "Lüqian had faults and would not reform; your servant had no choice but to impeach him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again praised his impeachment of Zhao Lüqian as apt. Chenglong said, "Lüqian would not mend his ways after repeated warnings; your servant had no choice but to denounce him."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「為政當知大體，小聰小察不足尚。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In governing one must know the larger pattern; petty cleverness and petty scrutiny are not to be esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Governing means grasping the larger design—petty cleverness and petty scrutiny are not to be prized.

sentences.zh: 人貴始終一節，爾其勉旃！」

translations.literal: What is prized in a man is constancy from beginning to end; do your utmost!"
translations.idiomatic: What matters is constancy from first to last—press on!"

sentences.zh: 旋賜帑金千、親乘良馬一，制詩褒寵，並命戶部遣官助成龍賑濟宣化等處饑民。

translations.literal: Immediately he was granted a thousand taels from the treasury, one fine horse from the emperor's own mount, and an imperial poem in praise and favor; he was also ordered that the Ministry of Revenue send officials to assist Chenglong in relieving famine among the hungry people of Xuanhua and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then granted him a thousand taels from the treasury, a fine horse from the imperial stables, and a poem of praise, and ordered the Ministry of Revenue to dispatch officials to help Chenglong relieve famine in Xuanhua and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 成龍复疏請緩真定府屬五縣房租，並全蠲霸州本年錢糧，均報可。

translations.literal: Chenglong again memorialized requesting deferment of house rents in the five counties subordinate to Zhending prefecture, and complete remission of Baozhou's land tax and grain levy for that year; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong also petitioned to defer house rents in five Zhending counties and to remit Baozhou's full tax assessment for the year; both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，乞假喪母，優詔許之。

translations.literal: That winter he requested leave to mourn his mother, and an edict of special favor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he asked leave to mourn his mother, and the throne graciously granted it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷江南江西總督。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 成龍先後疏薦直隸守道董秉忠、阜城知縣王燮、南路通判陳天棟。

translations.literal: Chenglong had in succession memorialized recommending the Zhili circuit defender Dong Bingzhong, the Fucheng magistrate Wang Xie, and the southern-route sub-prefect Chen Tiandong.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving Zhili, Chenglong had recommended Circuit Intendant Dong Bingzhong, Fucheng Magistrate Wang Xie, and Southern Route Sub-Prefect Chen Tiandong.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，复薦通州知州-{于}-成龍等。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he again recommended the Tongzhou prefect Yu Chenglong and others.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure he again recommended Tongzhou Prefect Yu Chenglong and others.

sentences.zh: 會江寧知府缺，命即以通州知州-{于}-成龍擢補。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jiangning prefecture post was vacant, and he was ordered to promote the Tongzhou prefect Yu Chenglong directly to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangning prefecture fell vacant, the court promoted Tongzhou Prefect Yu Chenglong to fill the post.

sentences.zh: 成龍至江南，進屬吏誥誡之。

translations.literal: When Chenglong arrived in Jiangnan he advanced to admonish his subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Jiangnan, Chenglong summoned his subordinates and lectured them sternly on their duties.

sentences.zh: 革加派，剔積弊，治事嘗至達旦。

translations.literal: He abolished surcharges, rooted out accumulated abuses, and in handling affairs often worked until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished illegal surcharges, uprooted entrenched abuses, and often worked on state business until dawn.

sentences.zh: 好微行，察知民間疾苦、屬吏賢不肖。

translations.literal: He liked to travel in disguise and learn the people's hardships and whether his subordinates were worthy or unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to go about incognito, learning firsthand of the people's hardships and which subordinates were fit for office.

sentences.zh: 自奉簡陋，日惟以粗糲蔬食自給。

translations.literal: His own manner of living was plain and spare; each day he had only coarse grain and vegetables to sustain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lived austerely, sustaining himself day after day on coarse grain and plain vegetables.

sentences.zh: 江南俗侈麗，相率易布衣。

translations.literal: The customs of Jiangnan were extravagant and ornate; people followed one another in changing to plain cloth garments.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan's taste for luxury faded as people followed his example and took to plain cotton dress.

sentences.zh: 士大夫家為減輿從、毀丹堊，婚嫁不用音樂，豪猾率家遠避。

translations.literal: Scholar-official households reduced their retinues and carriages and destroyed their red lacquer; weddings and funerals used no music; powerful scoundrels led their families to flee far away.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry families trimmed their retinues, stripped vermilion from their gates, and held weddings without music; powerful bullies fled the region with their kin.

sentences.zh: 居數月，政化大行。

translations.literal: Within a few months his civilizing influence was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Within months his reforms had transformed the region.

sentences.zh: 勢家懼其不利，構蜚語。

translations.literal: Powerful families feared he would harm their interests and fabricated slanderous talk.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families, fearing for their interests, spread malicious rumors against him.

sentences.zh: 明珠秉政，尤與忤。

translations.literal: Mingzhu held power in government and was especially at odds with him.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu Mingzhu held the reins of power and clashed with him above all.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，副都御史馬世濟督造漕船還京，劾成龍年衰，為中軍副將田萬侯所欺蔽。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the vice censor-in-chief Ma Shiji, having supervised construction of grain-transport ships and returned to the capital, impeached Chenglong as aged in years and deceived and screened by the deputy commander of the central army Tian Wanhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Vice Censor-in-Chief Ma Shiji, returning to the capital after supervising grain-barge construction, accused Chenglong of senility and of being misled by Central Army Deputy Commander Tian Wanhou.

sentences.zh: 命成龍回奏，成龍引咎乞嚴譴；

translations.literal: Chenglong was ordered to return and report; Chenglong took blame upon himself and begged for severe punishment;
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Chenglong to respond; he accepted blame and begged for severe punishment;

sentences.zh: 詔留任，萬侯降調。

translations.literal: an edict ordered him to remain in office, and Wanhou was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: but an edict kept him in post while Tian Wanhou was demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，江蘇巡撫-{余}-國柱入為左都御史，安徽巡撫徐國相遷湖廣總督，命成龍兼攝兩巡撫事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the Jiangsu provincial governor Yu Guozhu entered office as left censor-in-chief, the Anhui provincial governor Xu Guoxiang was transferred to governor-general of Huguang, and Chenglong was ordered to act concurrently in charge of the affairs of both provincial governors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Jiangsu Governor Yu Guozhu became left censor-in-chief and Anhui Governor Xu Guoxiang was moved to Huguang governor-general; Chenglong was ordered to act concurrently for both provinces.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 成龍歷官未嘗攜家屬，卒時，將軍、都統及僚吏入視，惟笥中綈袍一襲、床頭鹽豉數器而已。

translations.literal: Throughout his official career Chenglong had never brought his family with him; when he died, generals, commanders, and subordinate officials came to view him, and there was only a single silk robe in his chest and a few vessels of salt and fermented beans at the head of his bed.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong had never brought his family on any posting; when he died, generals, banner commanders, and staff came to view his effects and found only one silk robe in his trunk and a few dishes of salt and fermented beans beside his bed.

sentences.zh: 民罷市聚哭，家繪像祀之。

translations.literal: The people closed the markets and gathered to weep; households painted his portrait to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people shut their shops and gathered to mourn; families painted his portrait for household worship.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，諡清端。

translations.literal: He was granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and given the posthumous title Qingduan.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted state funeral rites and the posthumous title Qingduan, "Clear and Upright."

sentences.zh: 內閣學士錫住勘海疆還，上詢成龍在官狀，錫住奏甚清廉，但因輕信，或為屬員欺罔。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat academician Xizhu, returning from inspecting the maritime frontier, was asked by the emperor about Chenglong's conduct in office; Xizhu submitted that he was very honest and clean, but because he was too ready to trust others he was sometimes deceived by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretariat Academic Xizhu returned from inspecting the coast, the emperor asked about Chenglong's conduct in office. Xizhu reported that he had been exceptionally honest, though his trusting nature sometimes left him misled by subordinates.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「-{于}-成龍督江南，或言其變更素行，及卒後，始知其始終廉潔，為百姓所稱。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When Yu Chenglong supervised Jiangnan, some said he had changed his former conduct; only after his death was it known that from beginning to end he had been incorrupt, and was praised by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Yu Chenglong governed Jiangnan, some claimed he had abandoned his old ways; only after his death did people learn that he had been incorrupt from first to last, and the common people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 殆因素性鯁直，不肖挾仇讒害，造為此言耳。

translations.literal: This was probably because by nature he was bluntly upright, and unworthy men bore grudges and slandered him, fabricating such words.
translations.idiomatic: That was likely because he was bluntly upright by nature, and unworthy men who bore grudges against him invented such slanders.

sentences.zh: 居官如成龍，能有幾耶？」

translations.literal: Officials in office like Chenglong—how many can there be?"
translations.idiomatic: How many officials in office are there like Chenglong?"

sentences.zh: 是年冬，上南巡至江寧，諭知府於成龍曰：「爾務效前總督-{于}-成龍正直潔清，乃為不負。」

translations.literal: That winter the emperor toured south to Jiangning and instructed Prefect Yu Chenglong: "You must emulate the former governor Yu Chenglong in uprightness and clean integrity—only then will you not fail your charge."
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on his southern tour, the emperor reached Jiangning and told Prefect Yu Chenglong, "You must emulate the former governor Yu Chenglong in uprightness and integrity—that is how you will not betray your office."

sentences.zh: 又諭大學士等曰：「朕博採輿評，咸稱-{于}-成龍實天下廉吏第一。」

translations.literal: He also told the grand secretaries and others: "I have widely gathered popular opinion; all call Yu Chenglong truly the foremost incorrupt official under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the grand secretaries, "I have gathered opinion far and wide, and everyone agrees that Yu Chenglong is truly the foremost incorrupt official in the realm."

sentences.zh: 加贈太子太保，廕一子入監，復製詩褒之。

translations.literal: He was posthumously advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; one son was granted entrance to the Imperial Academy by privilege of office; the emperor again composed a poem to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, one son was granted admission to the Imperial Academy through hereditary privilege, and the emperor composed another poem in his praise.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he was enshrined in the Hall of Eminent Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign he was enshrined in the Hall of Eminent Worthies.

sentences.zh: 孫準，字子繩。

translations.literal: Sun Zhun, courtesy name Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhun, whose courtesy name was Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 自廕生授山東臨清知州，有清操。

translations.literal: Through privilege as the son of an enfeoffed official he was appointed magistrate of Linqing in Shandong; he had clean conduct.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of an enfeoffed official he entered office by privilege and was appointed magistrate of Linqing in Shandong, where he maintained a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，入為刑部員外郎，遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Recommended as outstanding, he entered the capital as a deputy director in the Ministry of Punishments and was promoted to a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding in performance, he was brought to the capital as a deputy director in the Ministry of Punishments and later promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出為江南驛鹽道，再遷浙江按察使，居成龍喪歸，起四川布政使。

translations.literal: He went out as Salt and Post Commissioner in Jiangnan, was again promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner in Zhejiang, returned home to observe mourning for Chenglong, and was then raised to financial commissioner in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Salt and Post Commissioner in Jiangnan, was promoted again to provincial surveillance commissioner in Zhejiang, went home to mourn Yu Chenglong, and was then recalled as financial commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十三年，授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of the Kangxi reign he was appointed governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 飭州縣立義學，令土司子弟及苗民俊秀者悉入肄業，送督學考試。

translations.literal: He ordered prefectures and counties to establish charity schools, had sons of tusi and talented Miao youths all enter to study, and sent them to the provincial education intendant for examination.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered prefectures and counties to establish charity schools, required the sons of native chiefs and promising Miao youths to enroll, and sent them to the provincial education intendant for examination.

sentences.zh: 調江蘇，歲饑，請發帑賑濟上元等十五縣及太倉、鎮海二衛。

translations.literal: Transferred to Jiangsu; famine struck that year; he requested disbursement from the treasury to relieve Shangyuan and fifteen other counties and the two garrisons of Taicang and Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jiangsu, he found famine that year and requested treasury funds to relieve Shangyuan and fifteen other counties, as well as the garrisons at Taicang and Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 濱江海田畝被潮汐衝擊，多坍沒，疏請豁免錢糧，詔允行。

translations.literal: Coastal and riverside fields were struck by tidal surges and largely washed away; he memorialized requesting exemption of tax and grain; an edict approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Fields along the coast and rivers were battered by tides and largely washed away; he memorialized for exemption of taxes and grain, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 以布政使宜思恭為總督噶禮所劾，準坐失察，罷歸。

translations.literal: Because Financial Commissioner Yi Sigong was impeached by Governor-General Gali, Zhun was punished for lax supervision and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Financial Commissioner Yi Sigong was impeached by Governor-General Gali, Zhun was held accountable for lax supervision, dismissed, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，復職銜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yongzheng reign his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 彭鵬，字奮斯，福建莆田人。

translations.literal: Peng Peng, courtesy name Fensi, a native of Putian in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng, whose courtesy name was Fensi, was a native of Putian in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 幼慧，有與其父仇，欲殺鵬，走匿得免。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever; someone bore a grudge against his father and wished to kill Peng Peng; he fled and hid and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever; a man who bore a grudge against his father tried to kill Peng Peng, but he fled into hiding and escaped.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年，舉鄉試。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Shunzhi reign he passed the provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠叛，迫就偽職，鵬陽狂示疾，椎齒出血，堅拒不從。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled he was compelled to accept a false office; Peng Peng feigned madness, showed illness, knocked out his teeth so they bled, and firmly refused to obey.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Peng Peng was forced to take a post under the rebel regime; he feigned madness and illness, knocked out his own teeth until they bled, and steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 事平，謁選，康熙二十三年，授三河知縣。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified he went up for appointment; in the twenty-third year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he presented himself for appointment, and in the twenty-third year of Kangxi he was made magistrate of Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 三河當衝要，旗、民雜居，號難治。

translations.literal: Sanhe lay on a major thoroughfare; bannermen and commoners lived mingled together; it was known as hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe stood on a major thoroughfare where banner troops and civilians lived side by side, and it had a reputation as a difficult county to govern.

sentences.zh: 鵬拊循懲勸，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Peng Peng comforted, punished, and admonished without fearing the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng soothed the people, punished wrongdoing, and exhorted them to reform, never flinching before the powerful.

sentences.zh: 有妄稱御前放鷹者，至縣索餼牽，鵬察其詐，縶而鞭之。

translations.literal: Someone falsely claimed to be on imperial orders to fly hawks; he came to the county to demand food for horses and servants; Peng Peng saw through the fraud, bound him, and flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: A man falsely claimed to be on imperial business flying hawks; he came to the county demanding fodder and attendants; Peng Peng exposed the fraud, bound him, and had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 治獄，摘發如神。

translations.literal: In handling lawsuits he exposed the facts as if by divinity.
translations.idiomatic: In handling lawsuits he uncovered the truth with uncanny skill.

sentences.zh: 鄰縣有疑獄，檄鵬往鞫，輒白其冤。

translations.literal: When a neighboring county had a doubtful case, they sent a dispatch for Peng Peng to interrogate, and he invariably cleared the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: When neighboring counties had doubtful cases, they would summon Peng Peng to try them, and he invariably cleared the innocent.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，聖祖巡畿甸，召問鵬居官及拒精忠偽命狀，賜帑金三百，諭曰：「知爾清正不受民錢，以此養爾廉，勝民間數萬多矣！」

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Sagely Ancestor toured the capital region, summoned him to ask about his conduct in office and his refusal of Geng Jingzhong's false commission, bestowed three hundred taels of treasury silver, and said: "Knowing that you are clean and upright and do not accept the people's money, use this to sustain your integrity—it is better than several tens of thousands from the people!"
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the Sagely Ancestor toured the capital region, summoned Peng Peng to ask about his conduct in office and his refusal of Geng Jingzhong's false commission, bestowed three hundred taels of treasury silver, and said, "I know you are upright and take no money from the people—use this to sustain your integrity; it is worth far more than the tens of thousands you might take from them!"

sentences.zh: 尋順天府尹許三禮劾鵬匿報控案，命巡撫-{于}-成龍察之。

translations.literal: Soon the Shuntian prefect Xu Sanli impeached Peng Peng for concealing and not reporting a petition case; the emperor ordered Governor Yu Chenglong to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shuntian Prefect Xu Sanli impeached Peng Peng for concealing a petition case and failing to report it; the emperor ordered Governor Yu Chenglong to investigate.

sentences.zh: 成龍奏：「鵬訊無左驗，方緝兇，非不報也。」

translations.literal: Chenglong memorialized: "Peng Peng's inquiry found no corroborating evidence; he was still hunting the culprit—it is not that he failed to report."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong reported, "Peng Peng's investigation found no corroborating evidence; he was still hunting the culprit—it is not that he failed to report the case."

sentences.zh: 吏議奪官，詔鐫級留任。

translations.literal: The Board of Civil Officials recommended dismissal; an edict reduced his rank but left him in post.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Civil Officials recommended dismissal, but an edict reduced his rank and allowed him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 嗣以緝盜不獲，累被議，積至降十三級，俱從寬留任。

translations.literal: Later because bandits were not captured he was repeatedly censured, accumulating to thirteen ranks reduced in all, each time leniently allowed to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he failed to capture bandits, he was censured again and again until his rank had been reduced thirteen levels in all, each time leniently allowed to keep his post.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，詔舉廉能吏，用尚書李天馥薦，鵬與邵嗣堯、陸隴其、趙蒼璧並行取，擢為科道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year an edict ordered recommendation of incorrupt and capable officials; on Ministry President Li Tianfu's recommendation, Peng Peng was taken together with Shao Siyao, Lu Longqi, and Zhao Cangbi and promoted to a censorate post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year an edict called for recommendations of incorrupt and capable officials; on the recommendation of Ministry President Li Tianfu, Peng Peng was selected together with Shao Siyao, Lu Longqi, and Zhao Cangbi and promoted to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 尋乞假歸，明年，即家起工科給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return; the next year he was raised from home to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested leave to return home, and the following year was recalled from his home to serve as supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，陝西西安、鳳翔，山西平陽災，發帑賑之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year disasters struck Xi'an and Fengxiang in Shaanxi and Pingyang in Shanxi; treasury funds were sent to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year disasters struck Xi'an and Fengxiang in Shaanxi and Pingyang in Shanxi, and treasury funds were dispatched for relief.

sentences.zh: 又命運河南米十萬石畀陝西散饑民。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to transport one hundred thousand shi of Henan grain to Shaanxi to distribute to famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to transport one hundred thousand shi of grain from Henan to Shaanxi for distribution to famine victims.

sentences.zh: 鵬疏論陝西、山西、河南三省有司不恤民狀，語甚切，下所司，並令鵬指實以聞。

translations.literal: Peng Peng memorialized criticizing officials in Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Henan for not caring for the people, with very urgent language; it was sent to the responsible departments and Peng Peng was also ordered to report specifics.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng memorialized on how officials in Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Henan were neglecting the people, in language so urgent it was sent to the responsible agencies and he was ordered to name the guilty parties.

sentences.zh: 鵬因奏涇陽知縣劉桂剋扣籽粒，猗氏知縣李澍杖殺災民，磁州知州陳成郊濫派運價，夏邑知縣尚崇震派銀包運，南陽知府硃璘曖昧分肥，並及聞喜、夏縣匿災不報狀。

translations.literal: Peng Peng then memorialized that Jingyang Magistrate Liu Gui withheld seed grain, Yishi Magistrate Li Shu beat famine victims to death, Cizhou Prefect Chen Chengjiao levied transport costs wantonly, Xiayi Magistrate Shang Chongzhen assigned silver for transport in lump sums, Nanyang Prefect Zhu Lin divided spoils ambiguously, and also the cases of Wenxi and Xia county concealing disaster without reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng then reported that Jingyang Magistrate Liu Gui had withheld seed grain, Yishi Magistrate Li Shu had beaten famine victims to death, Cizhou Prefect Chen Chengjiao had levied transport fees recklessly, Xiayi Magistrate Shang Chongzhen had assigned silver in lump sums for transport, Nanyang Prefect Zhu Lin had divided spoils in murky fashion, and that Wenxi and Xia counties had concealed the disaster without reporting it.

sentences.zh: 詔三省巡撫察審，事不皆實，鵬例當譴，上貰之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the three provincial governors to investigate; the matters were not all factual; by rule Peng Peng should have been punished, but the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the governors of the three provinces to investigate; not all the charges proved true, and though by rule Peng Peng should have been punished, the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，疏劾順天鄉試中式舉人李仙湄闈墨刪改過多，楊文鐸文謬妄，給事中馬士芳磨勘通賄。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he memorialized impeaching metropolitan graduate Li Xianmei for excessive deletion and alteration in his examination papers, Yang Wenduo for absurd errors in his essay, and supervising secretary Ma Shifang for collusion in the review through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he memorialized impeaching metropolitan examination graduate Li Xianmei for excessive deletions and alterations in his examination papers, Yang Wenduo for absurd errors in his essay, and supervising secretary Ma Shifang for bribery in the review process.

sentences.zh: 下九卿等察議，以鵬奏涉虛，因摘疏語有「臣言如妄，請劈臣頭，半懸國門，半懸順天府學」，以為狂妄不敬，應奪官。

translations.literal: The Nine Ministers and others were ordered to deliberate; because Peng Peng's memorial involved falsehoods, and because his memorial contained the phrase "If my words are false, let my head be split in two, half hung at the national gate and half at the Shuntian prefectural school," as arrogant disrespect, dismissal was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent to the Nine Ministers for deliberation; because Peng Peng's charges were not wholly substantiated, and because his memorial contained the words, "If I speak falsely, let my head be split in two, half hung at the national gate and half at the Shuntian prefectural school," they deemed this arrogant and disrespectful and recommended dismissal.

sentences.zh: 命鵬回奏，鵬疏言：「會議諸臣，徇試官徐倬、彭殿元欺飾，反以臣為妄，乞賜罪斥。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Peng Peng to reply; Peng Peng memorialized: "The ministers in conference, indulging the examiners Xu Chuo and Peng Dianyuan in concealment and misrepresentation, instead call me false; I beg to be punished and dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Peng Peng to respond; he memorialized, "The ministers in conference indulged the examiners Xu Chuo and Peng Dianyuan in concealment and deceit, yet call me the liar; I beg to be punished and dismissed."

sentences.zh: 上不問，而予倬、殿元休致。

translations.literal: The emperor did not pursue it but granted Xu Chuo and Peng Dianyuan retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no action against Peng Peng but granted Xu Chuo and Peng Dianyuan retirement.

sentences.zh: 是年，順天學政侍郎李光地遭母喪，上命在任守制，光地乞假九月。

translations.literal: That year Educational Commissioner of Shuntian Vice President Li Guangdi suffered his mother's death; the emperor ordered him to remain in office during mourning; Guangdi begged nine months' leave.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shuntian Education Commissioner and Vice President Li Guangdi lost his mother; the emperor ordered him to remain in office while observing mourning, but Guangdi requested nine months' leave.

sentences.zh: 鵬劾光地貪戀祿位，不請終制，應將光地解任，留京守制，上從之。

translations.literal: Peng Peng impeached Guangdi for clinging to salary and rank, not requesting full mourning; Guangdi should be removed from office and kept in the capital to observe mourning; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng impeached Guangdi for clinging to his salary and rank and failing to request the full mourning period; Guangdi should be removed from office and kept in the capital to observe mourning, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會廷臣集議，鵬追論楊文鐸文謬妄，與廷臣忿爭，事聞，命解職，以原品效力江南河工。

translations.literal: When court officials met in conference, Peng Peng pursued again Yang Wenduo's absurd essay and quarreled furiously with the officials; when it was reported, he was ordered dismissed and to serve on Jiangnan river works at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: At a gathering of court officials Peng Peng again pressed the charge against Yang Wenduo's absurd essay and quarreled furiously with his colleagues; when the matter was reported, he was dismissed and ordered to serve on Jiangnan river works at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，召授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was summoned and appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he was summoned and appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，出為貴州按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he went out as provincial surveillance commissioner in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督郭琇請除學政積弊，給事中慕琛、滿晉，御史鄭惟孜等亦疏列順天鄉試事。

translations.literal: Huguang Governor-General Guo Xiu requested removal of abuses in the education intendantcy; supervising secretaries Mu Chen and Man Jin, and censor Zheng Weizi, also memorialized listing matters of the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Governor-General Guo Xiu memorialized to remove longstanding abuses in the education intendantcy; supervising secretaries Mu Chen and Man Jin, and censor Zheng Weizi, also submitted memorials on the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 上以李光地。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Li Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Li Guangdi.

sentences.zh: 張鵬翮、郭琇與鵬俱清廉，命各抒所見。

translations.literal: Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng were all clean and upright; he ordered each to set forth his views.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng were all known for integrity; the emperor ordered each to set forth his views.

sentences.zh: 鵬疏言：「琇請嚴督撫處分，學政貪贓，提問督撫，需索陋規，視貪贓治罪，久有定例，請敕榜示律條。

translations.literal: Peng Peng memorialized: "Xiu requests strict punishment of governors and governors-general; when education intendants are greedy, governors should be questioned; demanding customary fees—there are long-standing statutes treating it like corruption; request an edict posting the legal articles.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng memorialized, "Guo Xiu asks for strict punishment of governors and governors-general when education intendants are corrupt; demanding customary fees has long been treated as corruption under established statutes—please issue an edict posting the relevant legal articles.

sentences.zh: 維孜請令各省監生回籍鄉試，九卿慮成均空虛，應責成祭酒司業，就坐監讀書者講習考課，各省學政擇諸生有文行者送入成均，何慮空虛？

translations.literal: Weizi requests that supervising students in the provinces return home for provincial examinations; the Nine Ministers fear the Imperial College would be emptied; they should charge the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor to lecture and examine those who remain; provincial education intendants should select literati students of literary merit to send to the college—why fear emptiness?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Weizi asks that provincial supervising students return home for the provincial examinations; the Nine Ministers fear the Imperial College would be emptied—but charge the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor to lecture and examine those who remain, and let provincial education intendants select promising students to send to the college. Why should it be empty?

sentences.zh: 琛、晉請察封坐號以防換卷，臣謂換卷多在入門暗約出號交卷時，請嚴稽於此。」

translations.literal: Chen and Jin request inspecting sealed seat numbers to prevent changing papers; I say changing papers mostly happens at the dark moment of agreeing numbers at entry and handing in papers at exit—request strict checking at these points."
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chen and Man Jin ask to inspect sealed seat numbers to prevent paper-switching; I believe switching mostly occurs when candidates secretly agree numbers at entry and exchange papers at submission—please enforce strict checks at those moments."

sentences.zh: 又言：「文官子弟請皇上親試，臣謂當另立考場，去取聽睿裁。」

translations.literal: He also said: "For sons of civil officials the emperor's personal examination is requested; I say a separate examination ground should be set up, acceptance and rejection left to imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Some ask that sons of civil officials be examined by the emperor in person; I believe a separate examination ground should be established, with acceptance and rejection left to imperial judgment."

sentences.zh: 與光地等疏皆下九卿詳議。

translations.literal: Memorials of Guangdi and others were all sent down to the Nine Ministers for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials of Li Guangdi and the others were all sent to the Nine Ministers for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 互詳光地等傳。

translations.literal: Cross-reference to the biographies of Li Guangdi and others.
translations.idiomatic: See the biographies of Li Guangdi and the others for further detail.

sentences.zh: 時河南巡撫徐潮之任，上諭曰：「爾能如李光地、張鵬翮、郭琇、彭鵬，不但為今之名臣，亦足重於後世矣。」

translations.literal: When Henan Governor Xu Chao took office, the emperor instructed him: "If you can be like Li Guangdi, Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng, you will not only be a famous minister today but also weigh heavy in later ages."
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Chao took office as governor of Henan, the emperor told him, "If you can be like Li Guangdi, Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng, you will be not only a famous minister in your own day but one whose name will carry weight for generations."

sentences.zh: 鵬在官省刑布德，減稅輕徭。

translations.literal: Peng Peng in office reduced punishment and spread virtue, lowered taxes and lightened corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In office Peng Peng reduced punishments and spread benevolent rule, cut taxes, and lightened corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 廣西舊供魚膠、鐵葉，非其土物，赴廣東採運，鵬疏請免之。

translations.literal: Guangxi formerly supplied fish glue and iron leaf, not products of that province; they were procured and transported from Guangdong; Peng memorialized to request exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi had formerly been required to supply fish glue and iron leaf—products not native to the province—and had to procure them from Guangdong; Peng memorialized to have the obligation lifted.

sentences.zh: 尋移撫廣東，瀕行，疏言：「廣西州縣藉端私派，名曰均平。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Guangdong; on the eve of departure he memorialized: "Guangxi prefectures and counties used pretexts for private levies called 'equalization.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Guangdong, and on the eve of his departure memorialized, "Guangxi prefectures and counties had used pretexts for private levies called 'equalization.

sentences.zh: 臣到任，劾罷賀縣、荔浦、懷集、武緣諸貪吏。

translations.literal: When I took office I impeached and dismissed corrupt officials of He county, Lipu, Huaiji, Wuyuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When I took office I impeached and dismissed corrupt officials in He, Lipu, Huaiji, Wuyuan, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 前此諸州縣大者派至三千兩，其次一二千兩。

translations.literal: Previously the larger prefectures and counties levied up to three thousand taels, the next rank one or two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the larger prefectures and counties had levied as much as three thousand taels, and smaller ones one or two thousand.

sentences.zh: 不肖官吏，往往先徵均平而後正課，甚者均平入己，遇事復行苛派。

translations.literal: Unworthy officials often collected equalization first and only then the regular taxes; worse, some kept equalization for themselves and when matters arose imposed harsh levies again.
translations.idiomatic: Unscrupulous officials often collected the equalization levy before the regular taxes; worse still, some pocketed the equalization funds and then imposed harsh levies when new needs arose.

sentences.zh: 其不派均平者，又取盈於火耗。

translations.literal: Those who did not levy equalization took surplus from the melt-and-cast fees.
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not levy equalization took their surplus from the melt-and-cast surcharge instead.

sentences.zh: 且均平所入，費於公者十​​之二三，費於饋遺者十之六七。

translations.literal: Moreover, of what equalization brought in, two or three tenths went to public use, six or seven tenths to gifts and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, of the equalization funds collected, only two or three tenths went to public purposes; six or seven tenths went to gifts and entertainment.

sentences.zh: 欲去舊弊、甦民困，必先養州縣之廉。

translations.literal: To remove old abuses and relieve the people's hardship, one must first nurture officials' integrity at the prefectural and county level.
translations.idiomatic: To remove these old abuses and relieve the people's hardship, one must first ensure that prefectural and county officials can live with integrity.

sentences.zh: 請於徵糧之內，明加火耗一分。

translations.literal: Request that within grain collection one fen of melt-and-cast surcharge be openly added.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that one fen of melt-and-cast surcharge be openly added within the grain tax collection.

sentences.zh: 其餘陋規，概行禁止。」

translations.literal: All other irregular fees should be entirely forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: All other irregular fees should be entirely prohibited."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下部議，謂火耗不可行，但嚴禁加派。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered the ministry deliberated, saying melt-and-cast surcharge could not be implemented but only strict prohibition of extra levies.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the ministry deliberated and ruled that the melt-and-cast surcharge could not be adopted, but that extra levies must be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 廣西舊未設武科，鵬奏請行之。

translations.literal: Guangxi had not formerly had military examinations; Peng memorialized to establish them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi had never held military examinations; Peng memorialized to establish them.

sentences.zh: 時與蕭永藻互調，上勉永藻效鵬，又諭大學士曰：「彭鵬人才壯健，前知三河，聞有賊，即佩刀乘馬馳捕，朕所知也。」

translations.literal: At that time he was mutually transferred with Xiao Yongzao; the emperor urged Yongzao to emulate Peng, and also told the grand secretaries: "Peng Peng's talent is robust; formerly as magistrate of Sanhe, when he heard of bandits he girded on a sword, mounted a horse, and galloped to capture—I know this of him."
translations.idiomatic: At that time he was transferred in a mutual exchange with Xiao Yongzao; the emperor urged Yongzao to emulate Peng Peng, and told the grand secretaries, "Peng Peng is a man of vigorous talent; when he was magistrate of Sanhe and heard of bandits, he would gird on his sword, mount his horse, and gallop out to capture them—I know this from personal knowledge."

sentences.zh: 御史王度昭劾鵬在廣西知布政使教化新虧帑，不即糾舉；

translations.literal: Censor Wang Duzhao impeached Peng: in Guangxi he knew Financial Commissioner Jiaohua Xin had depleted the treasury but did not immediately impeach;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Duzhao impeached Peng Peng, charging that in Guangxi he had known Financial Commissioner Jiaohua Xin had depleted the treasury but failed to impeach him at once;

sentences.zh: 迨離任始奏聞，又掩護其半。

translations.literal: only when leaving office did he report, and moreover concealed half.
translations.idiomatic: he reported the matter only when leaving office, and even then concealed half the loss.

sentences.zh: 廣西糧道張天覺改徵兵米浮銷九十餘萬，部勒追完，而鵬反以天覺署布政使。

translations.literal: Guangxi Grain Commissioner Zhang Tianjue changed collection of soldier grain and fraudulently consumed more than nine hundred thousand; the ministry ordered recovery; yet Peng instead appointed Tianjue acting financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Grain Commissioner Zhang Tianjue had altered the collection of soldier grain and fraudulently misappropriated more than nine hundred thousand; the ministry ordered full recovery, yet Peng Peng appointed Tianjue acting financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 兵米之案，必由籓司審詳，是直以天覺察天覺也。

translations.literal: The soldier-grain case must be scrutinized by the provincial treasurer—this is literally having Tianjue investigate Tianjue.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier-grain case had to be reviewed by the provincial treasurer—this amounted to having Tianjue investigate himself.

sentences.zh: 命鵬回契，鵬疏辨，並訐度昭。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Peng to respond with a memorial; Peng memorialized in defense and also denounced Duzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Peng Peng to submit a memorial in reply; Peng defended himself in a memorial and also denounced Wang Duzhao.

sentences.zh: 上以其辭忿激，降旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his language was furious, issued a stern edict of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding his language too heated, issued a stern edict of admonition.

sentences.zh: 廣東因借兵餉，改額賦徵銀為徵米，較估報時值浮多，戶部屢飭追完。

translations.literal: Guangdong because of borrowing military pay changed quota grain tax from silver collection to grain collection; compared with estimated prices at reporting time it was excessively high; the Ministry of Revenue repeatedly ordered recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong, having borrowed military funds, had changed quota grain taxes from silver to grain collection; compared with prices at the time of the original estimate, the amounts were far too high, and the Ministry of Revenue repeatedly ordered full recovery.

sentences.zh: 鵬至官，是年歲稔米價低，以米計銀少七萬三千有奇，疏請令經管各官扣追存庫，並議嗣後額賦仍依原則徵銀，採購兵米；

translations.literal: When Peng took office, that year the harvest was good and grain prices low; converting grain to silver amounted to seventy-three thousand odd taels less; he memorialized requesting responsible officials deduct and recover to store in the treasury, and also proposed that hereafter quota grain still be collected in silver per original rule while soldier grain was purchased;
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Peng took office that year the harvest was good and grain prices low; reckoned in silver, the grain tax came to an odd remainder of more than seventy-three thousand taels less than expected; he memorialized that responsible officials should deduct and recover the surplus to the treasury, and proposed that hereafter quota grain be collected in silver as before while soldier grain be purchased separately;

sentences.zh: 其按年應追完之銀，實因豐歉不同，米價無定，乞免重追：詔允行。

translations.literal: silver recoverable each year in fact varied with abundance or scarcity and grain prices were unfixed; he begged exemption from repeated recovery: an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: the silver recoverable each year in fact varied with harvests and grain prices were never fixed; he begged exemption from repeated recovery, and an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 鵬視事勤敏，遇墨吏糾劾無少徇。

translations.literal: Peng was diligent and keen in administration; when corrupt officials were impeached he showed no favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng administered affairs with diligence and alertness; when he impeached corrupt officials he showed no favoritism whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，步禱日中，詣獄慮囚，開倉平糶，旋得雨，民大稱頌。

translations.literal: In drought he prayed on foot in the midday sun, visited the prisons to consider prisoners, opened granaries for fair-price sale; rain soon came and the people greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he prayed on foot under the midday sun, visited the prisons to review cases, and opened granaries for fair-price grain sales; rain soon followed, and the people praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，卒官，年六十八，上深悼惜，稱其勤勞，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he died in office at age sixty-eight; the emperor deeply mourned, praised his diligence, and bestowed sacrificial rites and funeral honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he died in office at the age of sixty-eight; the emperor mourned him deeply, praised his diligence, and bestowed sacrificial rites and funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 尋祀廣東名宦。

translations.literal: Soon he was enshrined among Guangdong's famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon enshrined among Guangdong's famous officials.

sentences.zh: 陳瑸，字眉川，廣東海康人。

translations.literal: Chen Bin, courtesy name Meichuan, a native of Haikang in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin, whose courtesy name was Meichuan, was a native of Haikang in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十三年進士，授福建古田知縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-third year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Gutian in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the thirty-third year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Gutian in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 古田多山，丁田淆錯，賦役輕重不均，民逋逃遷徙，黠者去為盜。

translations.literal: Gutian was mostly mountains; household registers and fields were confused; tax and labor were unevenly heavy or light; people fled and migrated; the cunning became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Gutian was a mountainous county where household registers and land records were confused, taxes and labor obligations unevenly assessed, and people fled or migrated; the cunning among them turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 瑸請平賦役，民以蘇息。

translations.literal: Chen requested leveling of taxes and labor; the people were thereby relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin memorialized to equalize taxes and labor obligations, and the people were thereby relieved.

sentences.zh: 調台灣，台灣初隸版圖，民驍悍不馴。

translations.literal: Transferred to Taiwan; Taiwan had only lately been brought under the map; the people were fierce and hard to tame.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Taiwan, which had only recently been incorporated into the empire, he found a people fierce and difficult to govern.

sentences.zh: 瑸興學廣教，在縣五年，民知禮讓。

translations.literal: Chen promoted study and broad education; in five years as magistrate the people knew ritual and deference.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin promoted schools and broad education; within five years as magistrate the people had learned ritual and deference.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，行取，授刑部主事，歷郎中，出為四川提學道僉事。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year selected for capital office; appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, rose to director, went out as education intendant in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he was selected for capital office, appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, rose to director, and was then sent out as education intendant in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 清介公慎，杜絕苞苴。

translations.literal: Pure, restrained, and publicly cautious; he entirely cut off gift-giving.
translations.idiomatic: Pure, restrained, and scrupulously cautious in public affairs, he cut off gift-giving entirely.

sentences.zh: 上以四川官吏加派厲民，詔戒飭，特稱瑸廉。

translations.literal: The emperor because Sichuan officials imposed extra levies and harmed the people issued edicts of warning; he especially praised Chen's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sichuan officials were imposing extra levies that harmed the people, the emperor issued edicts of warning and singled out Chen Bin for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 未幾，用福建巡撫張伯行薦，調台灣廈門道。

translations.literal: Before long, on Fujian Governor Zhang Boxing's recommendation, he was transferred to Taiwan-Xiamen circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on the recommendation of Fujian Governor Zhang Boxing, he was transferred to the Taiwan-Xiamen circuit intendant post.

sentences.zh: 新學宮建硃子祠於學右，以正學厲俗，鎮以廉靜，番、民帖然。

translations.literal: The new Confucian temple built a Zhu Xi shrine to the right of the academy to correct learning and improve custom; he governed with clean stillness; aborigines and settlers were docile.
translations.idiomatic: At the new Confucian academy he built a shrine to Zhu Xi on its right side to uphold learning and improve local custom; governing with integrity and calm, he kept both aborigines and settlers docile.

sentences.zh: 在官應得公使錢，悉屏不取。

translations.literal: Public expense money due to him in office he entirely refused to take.
translations.idiomatic: All public expense allowances due him in office he refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，超擢偏沅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he was exceptionally promoted to governor of Bianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he was exceptionally promoted to governor of Bianyuan.

sentences.zh: 蒞任，劾湘潭知縣王爰溱縱役累民，長沙知府薛琳聲徇庇不糾劾，降黜有差。

translations.literal: On taking office he impeached Xiangtan Magistrate Wang Aizhen for letting runners oppress the people; Changsha Prefect Xue Linsheng was partial in shielding him and did not impeach; demotions and dismissals were meted out in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Upon assuming office he impeached Wang Aizhen, magistrate of Xiangtan, for allowing runners to oppress the people, and Xue Linsheng, prefect of Changsha, for shielding him instead of bringing charges; each was demoted or dismissed according to his offense.

sentences.zh: 尋條奏禁加耗，除酷刑，糶積穀，置社倉，崇節儉，禁餽送，先起運，興書院，飭武備，停開採，凡十事。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized in separate items: banning surcharges, abolishing cruel punishments, selling stored grain, establishing community granaries, honoring frugality, forbidding gift-giving, advancing grain transport, founding academies, rectifying military readiness, and halting mining—ten matters in all.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted a detailed memorial proposing ten measures: ban surcharges, abolish cruel punishments, sell stored grain, establish community granaries, promote frugality, forbid gift-giving, advance grain transport, found academies, strengthen military readiness, and halt mining.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉勉，諭以躬行實踐，勿騖虛名。

translations.literal: An edict praised and encouraged him, instructing him to practice personally in deed and not chase empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict of praise and encouragement, urging him to put reforms into practice himself and not chase empty reputation.

sentences.zh: 旋入覲，奏言：「官吏妄取一錢，即與百千萬金無異。

translations.literal: Soon he came to audience and submitted: "If an official recklessly takes even one cash, it is no different from taking millions in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he attended court and said, "When an official recklessly takes even a single cash, it is no different from seizing millions in gold.

sentences.zh: 人所以貪取，皆為用不足。

translations.literal: The reason people greedily take is that their expenses are insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: People steal because their legitimate expenses are not covered.

sentences.zh: 臣初任知縣，即不至窮苦，不取一錢，亦自足用。」

translations.literal: When your servant first served as magistrate, he did not reach destitution; taking not one cash, he still had enough for use."
translations.idiomatic: When I first served as a magistrate I was never reduced to want; without taking a single cash I still had enough to live on."

sentences.zh: 比退，上目之曰：「此苦行老僧也！」

translations.literal: When he had withdrawn, the emperor fixed his eyes on him and said: "This is an old monk practicing austerities!"
translations.idiomatic: When he withdrew, the emperor watched him go and said, "There goes an old monk living on austerities!"

sentences.zh: 尋調撫福建，上諭廷臣曰：「朕見瑸，察其舉止言論，實為清官。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Fujian; the emperor instructed the court ministers: "I have seen Chen and observed his bearing and speech—he is truly an honest official.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to governor of Fujian. The emperor told the court ministers, "I have met Chen Bin and observed his bearing and speech—he is truly an honest official.
