sentences.zh: 瑸生長海濱，非世家大族，無門生故舊，而天下皆稱其清。

translations.literal: Chen grew up on the seacoast; he is not from a great clan or eminent house; he has no students or old associates, yet all under Heaven call him honest.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin grew up on the coast; he comes from no great clan and has no network of students or old associates, yet the whole empire calls him incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 非有實行，豈能如此？

translations.literal: Without real conduct in practice, how could it be so?
translations.idiomatic: Without genuine conduct in office, how could that be so?

sentences.zh: 國家得此等人，實為祥瑞。

translations.literal: For the state to obtain men like this is truly an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: For the dynasty to obtain such men is truly an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 宜加優異，以厲清操。」

translations.literal: He should receive added favor and distinction to encourage clean integrity."
translations.idiomatic: He should receive added honors to encourage others in clean integrity."

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上問：「福建有加耗否？」

translations.literal: At his farewell audience before leaving post, the emperor asked: "Does Fujian have surcharges?"
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor asked, "Does Fujian levy surcharges?"

sentences.zh: 瑸奏：「台灣三縣無之。」

translations.literal: Chen submitted: "The three counties of Taiwan have none."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin replied, "The three counties of Taiwan do not."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「火耗盡禁，州縣無以辦公，恐別生弊端。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If melting-loss allowances are entirely forbidden, prefectures and counties will have no means to conduct public business; I fear other abuses will arise."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If melting-loss allowances are banned entirely, prefectures and counties will have no funds for public business, and I fear new abuses will arise."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「清官誠善，惟以清而不刻為尚。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Honest officials are truly good, but what is to be esteemed is being honest without being harsh."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Honest officials are indeed admirable, but what matters is integrity without harshness.

sentences.zh: 瑸為治，舉大綱，不尚煩苛。

translations.literal: In governing, Chen grasped the larger outline and did not esteem troublesome severity.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin governed by grasping the larger outline and did not favor petty severity.

sentences.zh: 修建考亭書院及建陽、尤溪硃子祠，疏請御書榜額，並允之。

translations.literal: He rebuilt the Kaoting Academy and Zhu Xi shrines at Jianyang and Youxi, memorialized requesting imperial calligraphy for inscribed plaques, and all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the Kaoting Academy and Zhu Xi shrines at Jianyang and Youxi, petitioned for imperial calligraphy for their plaques, and the requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 复疏言：「防海賊與山賊異，山賊嘯聚有所，而海賊則出沒靡常。

translations.literal: Again he memorialized: "Defending against sea bandits differs from mountain bandits; mountain bandits gather and roar in fixed places, while sea bandits appear and vanish without constancy.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "Defending against pirates at sea differs from mountain bandits; mountain rebels gather in fixed haunts, but sea pirates appear and vanish without pattern.

sentences.zh: 台灣、金、廈防海賊，又與沿海邊境不同，沿海邊境患在突犯內境，而台、廈患在剽掠海中。

translations.literal: Defending Taiwan, Jinmen, and Xiamen against sea bandits again differs from the coastal frontier; the coastal frontier's trouble lies in sudden raids into the interior, while Taiwan and Xiamen's trouble lies in plunder on the open sea.
translations.idiomatic: Defending Taiwan, Jinmen, and Xiamen against pirates again differs from the general coast: on the mainland frontier the danger is sudden raids inland, whereas for Taiwan and Xiamen the danger is plunder on the open sea.

sentences.zh: 欲防颱、廈海賊，當令提標及台、澎水師定期會哨，以交旗為驗。

translations.literal: To defend against Taiwan and Xiamen sea bandits, the provincial commander and the Taiwan-Penghu naval forces should be ordered to hold regular joint patrols, with exchange of flags as verification.
translations.idiomatic: To guard Taiwan and Xiamen waters, the provincial commander and the Taiwan-Penghu naval forces should hold regular joint patrols, verified by exchanging flags.

sentences.zh: 商船出海，令台、廈兩汛撥哨船護送。

translations.literal: When merchant vessels put to sea, order the two garrisons of Taiwan and Xiamen to dispatch patrol boats to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant vessels putting to sea should be escorted by patrol boats dispatched from the Taiwan and Xiamen garrisons.

sentences.zh: 又令商船連環具結，遇賊首尾相救，不救以通同行劫論罪。」

translations.literal: Also order merchant vessels to bind themselves in linked groups; when bandits appear, bow and stern must rescue one another; failure to rescue is punished as complicity in joint robbery on the seas."
translations.idiomatic: Merchant ships should also bind themselves in convoys; when pirates attack, every vessel must aid the others, and any refusal is to be punished as complicity in piracy."

sentences.zh: 下部議，以為繁瑣，上韙其言，命九卿再議，允行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation; they deemed it cumbersome, but the emperor approved his words, ordered the Nine Ministers to deliberate again, and permitted implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deemed the plan cumbersome, but the emperor approved Chen Bin's proposal, ordered the Nine Ministers to reconsider, and allowed it to take effect.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，兼攝閩浙總督。

translations.literal: That winter he also served concurrently as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was also appointed acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 奉命巡海，自齎行糧，屏絕供億。

translations.literal: Ordered to patrol the sea, he brought his own traveling rations and entirely refused official supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to patrol the coast, he carried his own provisions and refused all official supplies.

sentences.zh: 捐穀應交巡撫公費，奏請充餉。

translations.literal: Grain he had donated that was due as the governor's public expense fund he memorialized requesting be applied to military rations.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that grain he had donated, which was due as the governor's public expense fund, be applied to military rations instead.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「督撫有以公費請充餉者，朕皆未之允。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When governors and governors-general have requested public expense funds for military rations, I have never approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Whenever governors have asked to divert public expense funds to military rations, I have refused.

sentences.zh: 蓋恐準令充餉，即同正項錢糧，不肖者又於此外婪取，重為民累。」

translations.literal: This is because I fear that if approval is given to apply them to rations, they will become the same as regular tax and grain levies, and unworthy men will again greedily take beyond this, heavily burdening the people anew."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once such funds are treated like regular tax revenue, unworthy officials will extort still more on top of them and the people will be burdened again."

sentences.zh: 令瑸遇本省需款撥用。

translations.literal: He ordered Chen, whenever funds were needed in his province, to allocate them for use.
translations.idiomatic: He told Chen Bin to draw on those funds whenever the province required money.

sentences.zh: 賓又請以司庫餘平賞賚兵役，命遵前旨。

translations.literal: Chen again requested using the treasury surplus from scale weighing to reward soldiers and runners; he was ordered to follow the previous instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin also asked to use treasury scale surpluses to reward soldiers and runners; the emperor ordered him to follow the earlier instruction.

sentences.zh: 廣東雷州東洋塘堤岸，海潮衝激，侵損民田，瑸奏請修築，即移所貯公項及俸錢助工費。

translations.literal: At Dongyang Pond embankment in Leizhou, Guangdong, sea tides struck and eroded the people's fields; Chen memorialized requesting repair and immediately transferred stored public funds and his salary to assist the labor costs.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongyang Pond in Leizhou, Guangdong, tidal surges were eroding farmland; Chen Bin petitioned to rebuild the dike and immediately diverted his stored public funds and salary to cover the work.

sentences.zh: 堤岸自是永固，鄉人蒙其利。

translations.literal: The embankment was thereafter permanently secure, and the villagers received its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The dike thereafter stood firm, and the local people benefited from it.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，以病乞休，詔慰留之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, on grounds of illness he requested retirement; an edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he asked to retire on grounds of illness; an edict urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 遺疏以所貯公項餘銀一萬三千有奇充西師之費。

translations.literal: His final memorial offered the remaining silver of more than thirteen thousand taels in stored public funds for the western campaign's expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial he offered more than thirteen thousand taels of remaining public funds for the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 命以一萬佐餉，餘給其子為葬具。

translations.literal: He was ordered that ten thousand assist military rations and the remainder be given his son for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered ten thousand taels applied to military rations and the remainder given his son for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 尋諭大學士曰：「陳賓居官甚優，操守極清，朕所罕見，恐古人中亦不多得也。」

translations.literal: Soon he instructed the Grand Secretaries: "Chen Bin's conduct in office is very excellent and his integrity extremely clean—rarely seen by me; I fear that even among the ancients such men were not often found."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he told the Grand Secretaries, "Chen Bin's service has been outstanding and his integrity exceptionally rare in my experience; even among the ancients such men were seldom found.

sentences.zh: 追授禮部尚書，廕一子入監讀書，諡清端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites; one son was given hereditary privilege to enter the Imperial Academy; his posthumous title was Qingduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, one son was granted entry to the Imperial Academy, and he received the posthumous title Qingduan, "Clear and Upright."

sentences.zh: 瑸服禦儉素，自奉惟草具粗糲。

translations.literal: Chen's clothing was plain and simple; for his own upkeep he had only coarse vegetable fare.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin dressed plainly and lived on coarse vegetable fare.

sentences.zh: 居止皆於廳事，昧爽治事，夜分始休。

translations.literal: His dwelling and rest were all in the main hall; at daybreak he handled affairs and only at midnight did he rest.
translations.idiomatic: He lived and worked in the main hall, began business at daybreak, and rested only after midnight.

sentences.zh: 在福建置學田，增書院學舍，聘主講，人文日盛。

translations.literal: In Fujian he established school fields, increased academy dormitories, engaged lecturers, and letters and culture daily flourished.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian he endowed school lands, expanded academy buildings, hired lecturers, and local learning flourished day by day.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he was entered for worship in the Shrine of Eminent Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign he was enshrined in the Shrine of Eminent Worthies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，賜其孫子良舉人；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign his grandson Ziliang was granted the juren degree;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign his grandson Ziliang was granted the juren degree;

sentences.zh: 子恭員外郎，官至知府。

translations.literal: his son Zigong became a secretary in the outer service and rose to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: his son Zigong became an outer-service secretary and rose to prefect.

sentences.zh: 陳鵬年，字滄洲，湖廣湘潭人。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian, style name Cangzhou, was a native of Xiangtan in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian, style name Cangzhou, was a native of Xiangtan in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirtieth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the thirtieth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 授浙江西安知縣，當兵後，戶口流亡，豪強率佔田自殖。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Xi'an in Zhejiang; it was just after warfare; household registers had fled; powerful families mostly seized fields to cultivate for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Xi'an county in Zhejiang after the wars, he found the population dispersed and powerful families seizing abandoned fields for themselves.

sentences.zh: 鵬年履畝按驗，復業者數千戶。

translations.literal: Pengnian walked the fields and verified acre by acre; those who resumed cultivation numbered several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian walked the fields and verified holdings acre by acre, restoring several thousand households to their land.

sentences.zh: 烈婦徐冤死十年，鵬年雪其枉，得罪人置諸法。

translations.literal: The chaste widow Xu had been wrongfully killed for ten years; Pengnian cleared her injustice and placed the guilty under the law.
translations.idiomatic: The chaste widow Xu had been wrongfully executed ten years earlier; Chen Pengnian cleared her name and punished those responsible.

sentences.zh: 禁溺女，民感之，女欲棄复育者，皆以陳為姓。

translations.literal: He forbade drowning infant girls; the people were moved; girls about to be abandoned and then raised again were all given the surname Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade the drowning of infant girls; moved by his example, families who rescued abandoned daughters gave them the surname Chen.

sentences.zh: 河道總督張鵬翮薦調赴江南河工，授江南山陽知縣，遷海州知州。

translations.literal: Grand Canal Director Zhang Penghe recommended him transferred to Jiangnan river works; he was appointed magistrate of Shanyang in Jiangnan and promoted to prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal Director Zhang Penghe recommended him for Jiangnan river works; he was appointed magistrate of Shanyang and later promoted to prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，聖祖南巡閱河，以山東飢，詔截漕四萬石，令鵬翮選賢幹吏運兗州分賑，以鵬年董事，全活​​數万人。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year the Sacred Ancestor toured south to inspect the rivers; because Shandong was famine-stricken, an edict diverted forty thousand shi of tribute grain; Zhang Penghe was ordered to select capable officials to transport it to Yanzhou for distribution in relief; Pengnian directed the work and fully saved tens of thousands of people.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year the emperor toured south to inspect the rivers; with Shandong in famine, he ordered forty thousand shi of tribute grain diverted, Zhang Penghe to choose capable officials to transport it to Yanzhou for relief distribution, and Chen Pengnian to direct the effort, saving tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 上回鑾，召見濟寧舟次，賦詩稱旨，賜御書。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the imperial carriage, he summoned him at Jining on the boat route, composed a poem that pleased the emperor's intent, and was granted imperial calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey the emperor summoned him aboard at Jining, received a poem that pleased him, and granted imperial calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 尋擢江寧知府。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，上复南巡，總督阿山召屬吏議增地丁耗羨為巡幸供億，鵬年力持不可，事得寢。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year the emperor again toured south; Governor Ashan summoned subordinate officials to discuss increasing land-tax surcharges for the imperial tour's supplies; Pengnian strongly held that it could not be done, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year, on another southern tour, Governor Ashan summoned subordinates to discuss raising land-tax surcharges to fund the imperial visit; Chen Pengnian firmly opposed it and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 阿山嗛之，令主辦龍潭行宮，侍從徵餽遺，悉勿應，忌者中以蜚語。

translations.literal: Ashan resented him and ordered him to oversee the Longtan imperial lodge; attendants solicited gifts and he entirely refused to respond; jealous men struck him with slanderous talk.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan resented him and put him in charge of the Longtan imperial lodge; when attendants solicited gifts he refused them all, and jealous rivals spread slander.

sentences.zh: 會致仕大學士張英入對，上問江南廉吏，舉鵬年；

translations.literal: It happened that retired Grand Secretary Zhang Ying came to audience; the emperor asked about honest officials in Jiangnan and he named Pengnian;
translations.idiomatic: When retired Grand Secretary Zhang Ying attended court, the emperor asked about honest officials in Jiangnan and he named Chen Pengnian;

sentences.zh: 复詢居官狀，英言：「吏畏威而不怨，民懷德而不玩，士式教而不欺，廉其末也。」

translations.literal: again asked about his conduct in office; Ying said: "Clerks fear his authority yet do not resent him; the people cherish his virtue yet do not treat him lightly; scholars take his teaching as model yet are not deceived—integrity is the least of it."
translations.idiomatic: asked again about his conduct in office, Zhang Ying said, "Clerks fear his authority yet bear no grudge; the people cherish his virtue yet do not take liberties; scholars model themselves on his teaching without being deceived—integrity is the least of his gifts."

sentences.zh: 上意乃釋。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's suspicions were lifted.

sentences.zh: 幸京口閱水師，先一日，阿山檄鵬年於江乾疊石為步，江流急，施工困難，胥徒惶遽。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jingkou to review the naval forces, the day before Ashan dispatched an order to Pengnian to pile stones on the riverbank as a walkway; the current was swift and construction difficult; clerks and runners were alarmed and flustered.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's visit to Jingkou to review the fleet, Ashan ordered Chen Pengnian the day before to pile stones along the riverbank for a walkway; the current was swift, work was difficult, and clerks and runners panicked.

sentences.zh: 鵬年率士民親運土石，詰旦工成。

translations.literal: Pengnian led gentry and commoners personally to transport earth and stone; by dawn the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian led local gentry and commoners to haul earth and stone himself, and the work was finished by dawn.

sentences.zh: 顧阿山憾不已，疏劾鵬年受鹽、典各商年規，侵蝕龍江關稅銀，又無故枷責關役，坐奪職，系江寧獄。

translations.literal: Yet Ashan's resentment did not cease; he memorialized impeaching Pengnian for receiving annual payments from salt and pawn merchants, embezzling Longjiang customs tax silver, and also for groundlessly cangueing and punishing customs runners; on conviction his office was stripped and he was imprisoned in Jiangning jail.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ashan's resentment did not end; he impeached Chen Pengnian for taking annual payments from salt and pawn merchants, embezzling Longjiang customs revenue, and groundlessly punishing customs clerks; Chen Pengnian was stripped of office and imprisoned in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 命桑額、張鵬翮與阿山會鞫，江寧民呼號罷市，諸生千餘建幡將叩閽。

translations.literal: Sang'e, Zhang Penghe, and Ashan were ordered to conduct a joint inquest; Jiangning people cried out and closed the markets; more than a thousand students raised banners intending to petition at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Sang'e, Zhang Penghe, and Ashan were ordered to conduct a joint trial; the people of Jiangning wailed and shut their shops, and more than a thousand students raised banners to petition at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 鵬年嘗就南市樓故址建鄉約講堂，月朔宣講聖諭，並為之榜曰「天語丁寧」。

translations.literal: Pengnian had once built a village compact lecture hall on the old site of South Market Tower, on the first of each month proclaiming the Sacred Edicts, and also inscribed a plaque for it reading "Imperial words earnestly repeated."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian had built a village compact lecture hall on the old site of South Market Tower, where on the first of each month he proclaimed the Sacred Edicts, and hung a plaque reading "Imperial words earnestly repeated."

sentences.zh: 南市樓者故狹邪地也，因坐以大不敬，論大辟。

translations.literal: South Market Tower was formerly a place of narrow alleys and vice; on this charge he was convicted of grave disrespect and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Because South Market Tower had been a pleasure quarter, he was charged with grave disrespect and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 上與大學士李光地論阿山居官，光地言阿山任事廉幹，獨劾陳鵬年犯清議，上頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed Ashan's conduct in office with Grand Secretary Li Guangdi; Guangdi said Ashan was honest and capable in affairs but impeaching Chen Pengnian offended pure opinion; the emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed Ashan's service with Grand Secretary Li Guangdi, who said Ashan was honest and capable but that impeaching Chen Pengnian had offended public opinion; the emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 讞上，鵬年坐奪官免死，徵入武英殿修書。

translations.literal: When the verdict was submitted, Pengnian was convicted of stripping office yet spared death and was summoned to the Hall of Military Glory to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: When the verdict was submitted, Chen Pengnian was stripped of office but spared death and summoned to compile books in the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，復出為蘇州知府。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he again went out as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was again appointed prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 禁革奢俗，清滯獄，聽斷稱神。

translations.literal: He forbade and reformed extravagant customs, cleared backlog cases, and in hearing and deciding cases was called divine.
translations.idiomatic: He banned extravagant customs, cleared backlog cases, and was said to judge cases with uncanny insight.

sentences.zh: 值歲饑，疫甚，週曆村墟，詢民疾苦，請賑貨，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: It happened to be a famine year and epidemic was severe; he went round through villages and hamlets, inquired into the people's hardships, requested relief goods, and fully saved very many.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine and severe epidemic he toured villages to learn the people's hardships, secured relief supplies, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，署布政使。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he served as acting provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he served as acting provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張伯行雅重鵬年，事無鉅細，倚以裁決。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Boxing greatly esteemed Pengnian; in affairs great or small he relied on him for decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Boxing greatly valued Chen Pengnian and relied on him for decisions great and small.

sentences.zh: 總督噶禮與伯行忤，並忌鵬年。

translations.literal: Governor-General Gali was at odds with Boxing and likewise resented Pengnian.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Gali was at odds with Zhang Boxing and also resented Chen Pengnian.

sentences.zh: 已，劾布政使宜思恭、糧道賈樸，因坐鵬年覈報不實，吏議奪官，遣戍黑龍江，上寬之，命仍來京修書。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached Provincial Treasurer Yi Sigong and Grain Intendant Jia Pu; because Pengnian was implicated for false verification reports, the ministry officials deliberated stripping his office and sending him to exile in Heilongjiang; the emperor showed leniency and ordered him still to come to the capital to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gali impeached Provincial Treasurer Yi Sigong and Grain Intendant Jia Pu and implicated Chen Pengnian for false verification reports; the ministry recommended stripping his office and exiling him to Heilongjiang, but the emperor showed leniency and ordered him back to Beijing to compile books.

sentences.zh: 噶禮复密奏鵬年虎丘詩，以為怨望，欲文致其罪，上不報。

translations.literal: Gali again secretly memorialized Pengnian's Tiger Hill poem, taking it as resentment and disaffection, wishing to frame his crime in writing; the emperor did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Gali again secretly memorialized Chen Pengnian's Tiger Hill poem as evidence of resentment and tried to frame a charge, but the emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 俄，噶禮與伯行互訐，屢遣大臣按治，議奪伯行職。

translations.literal: Before long Gali and Boxing mutually impeached each other; the court repeatedly sent grand ministers to investigate and deliberate stripping Boxing's office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gali and Zhang Boxing impeached each other; the court repeatedly sent grand ministers to investigate, and they recommended stripping Zhang Boxing of office.

sentences.zh: 上以伯行清廉，命九卿改議，並諭曰：「噶禮曾奏陳鵬年詩語悖謬，宵人伎倆，大率如此。

translations.literal: Because the emperor knew Boxing was honest and clean, he ordered the Nine Ministers to revise their deliberation, and also instructed: "Gali once memorialized that Chen Pengnian's poem words were perverse and absurd—villainous men's tricks are mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zhang Boxing was incorrupt, the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to reconsider and said, "Gali once claimed Chen Pengnian's poem was seditious—such are the tricks of petty schemers.

sentences.zh: 朕豈受若輩欺耶？」

translations.literal: How could I be deceived by such people?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I can be fooled by such people?"

sentences.zh: 因出其詩畀閣臣共閱。

translations.literal: He thereupon produced the poem and gave it to the Grand Secretariat ministers to read together.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced the poem for the Grand Secretariat ministers to read together.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，出署霸昌道，仍回京修書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he went out to serve as acting intendant of Bachang circuit, then still returned to the capital to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he briefly served as acting intendant of Bachang circuit, then returned to Beijing to compile books.

sentences.zh: 六十年，命隨尚書張鵬翮勘山東、河南運河，時河決武陟縣馬營口，自長垣直注張秋，命河督趙世顯塞之。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was ordered to follow Minister Zhang Penghe in surveying the Grand Canal in Shandong and Henan; at the time the Yellow River burst at Mayingkou in Wuzhi county and from Changyuan poured straight into Zhangqiu; the Yellow River Director Zhao Shixian was ordered to block it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was ordered to accompany Minister Zhang Penghe in surveying the Shandong and Henan sections of the Grand Canal; the Yellow River had burst at Mayingkou in Wuzhi county and was pouring from Changyuan straight toward Zhangqiu, and River Director Zhao Shixian was ordered to seal the breach.

sentences.zh: 議久不決，鵬年疏言：「黃河老堤衝決八九里，大溜直趨溢口，宜於對岸上流廣武山下別開引河，更於決口稍東亦開引河，引溜仍歸正河，方可堵築。」

translations.literal: Deliberation long remained unsettled; Pengnian memorialized: "The Yellow River's old embankment was breached for eight or nine li; the main current rushed straight toward the spill mouth; on the opposite bank upstream below Mount Guangwu a diversion channel should be opened separately, and also slightly east of the breach another diversion should be opened, leading the current back to the main river—only then can blocking and building proceed."
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation dragged on; Chen Pengnian memorialized, "The old Yellow River dike had been breached for eight or nine li and the main current was rushing toward the spillway; a diversion should be cut below Mount Guangwu on the opposite bank upstream, and another slightly east of the breach, to lead the current back to the main channel before the dike could be rebuilt."

sentences.zh: 奏入稱旨。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it pleased the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial pleased the emperor when it was submitted.

sentences.zh: 世顯罷，即命鵬年署河道總督。

translations.literal: Shixian was dismissed and Pengnian was immediately ordered to serve as acting Grand Canal Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shixian was dismissed and Chen Pengnian was immediately appointed acting Grand Canal Director.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，馬營口既塞復決，鵬年謂：「地勢低窪，雖有引河，流不能暢。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, after Mayingkou had been blocked it burst again; Pengnian said: "The terrain is low and hollow; though there are diversion channels, the flow cannot run freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year, after Mayingkou had been sealed it burst again; Chen Pengnian said, "The terrain is low-lying; though diversion channels exist, the flow cannot run freely.

sentences.zh: 惟有分疏上下，殺其悍怒。

translations.literal: Only by dividing and diverting above and below can its fierce rage be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Only by dividing the current above and below can its fierce force be reduced.

sentences.zh: 請於沁、黃交匯對岸王家溝開引河，使水東南行，入滎澤正河，然後堤工可成。」

translations.literal: I request opening a diversion at Wangjiagou on the opposite bank where the Qin and Yellow rivers meet, causing the water to run southeast into the main channel of Yingze, and only then can dike works succeed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a diversion be cut at Wangjiagou on the opposite bank where the Qin and Yellow rivers meet, sending the water southeast into the main Yingze channel; only then can the dikes be completed."

sentences.zh: 詔如議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered implementation as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the plan carried out.

sentences.zh: 先是，馬營決口因桃汛流激，難以程工；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Maying breach because of the peach-blossom flood season's swift current made it hard to schedule the work;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, work at the Maying breach had been delayed because the spring flood current was too swift to schedule construction;

sentences.zh: 副都御史牛鈕奉命閱河，奏於上流秦家廠堵築，工甫竟，而南壩尾旋決一百二十餘丈，入馬營東下。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Niu Niu was ordered to inspect the rivers and memorialized blocking and building at Qinjiazhuang upstream; the work had just been finished when the southern dike tail immediately burst for more than a hundred and twenty zhang, entering Maying and flowing east.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Niu Niu was ordered to inspect the rivers and proposed blocking the current upstream at Qinjiazhuang; the work had barely finished when the southern dike tail burst for more than 120 zhang and the flood poured east through Maying.

sentences.zh: 鵬年與巡撫楊宗義謀合之。

translations.literal: Pengnian and Governor Yang Zongyi planned to join and close it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian and Governor Yang Zongyi planned to close the breach together.

sentences.zh: 既，北壩尾复潰百餘丈，鵬年乃建此議。

translations.literal: Afterward the northern dike tail again burst for more than a hundred zhang, and only then did Pengnian advance this proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Then the northern dike tail burst again for more than a hundred zhang, and Chen Pengnian advanced this proposal.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命真除。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was ordered to regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne, Chen Pengnian was confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 時南北壩尾合而復潰者四，至是以次合龍，而馬營口尚未塞。

translations.literal: At the time the northern and southern dike tails had been joined and burst again four times; by now they were joined in sequence, but Mayingkou was still not blocked.
translations.idiomatic: By then the northern and southern dike tails had been joined and breached again four times; they were now closed in sequence, but Mayingkou remained unsealed.

sentences.zh: 鵬年止宿河堧，寢食俱廢，浸羸憊。

translations.literal: Pengnian lodged on the river embankment; sleep and food were both abandoned, and he gradually grew emaciated and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian lodged on the riverbank, neglecting sleep and food until he grew gaunt and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，疾篤，遣御醫診視。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng his illness was grave and an imperial physician was dispatched to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng his illness grew grave and an imperial physician was sent to examine him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，上聞，諭曰：「鵬年積勞成疾，沒於公所。

translations.literal: Soon he died; when the emperor heard, he instructed: "Pengnian accumulated labor until illness and died at his public post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died; when the emperor heard, he said, "Chen Pengnian wore himself out in service and died at his post.

sentences.zh: 聞其家有八旬老母，室如懸罄。

translations.literal: I hear his family has an eighty-year-old mother and the house is as if emptied by a hanging vessel.
translations.idiomatic: I hear he leaves an eighty-year-old mother and a household with nothing in it.

sentences.zh: 此真鞠躬盡瘁、死而後已之臣。」

translations.literal: This is truly a minister who bent his body, exhausted his heart, and died only afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Such a minister truly devoted himself utterly and did not rest until death.

sentences.zh: 褒錫甚至。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The rewards and honors were extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 賜帑金二千，錫其母封誥，視一品例廕子，諡恪勤。

translations.literal: He was granted two thousand taels of treasury silver, his mother was bestowed a patent of nobility, his son was ennobled by precedent as for the first rank, and his posthumous title was Keqin.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted two thousand taels from the treasury, conferred a noble patent on his mother, ennobled his son according to first-rank precedent, and gave him the posthumous title Keqin.

sentences.zh: 祀河南、江寧名宦。

translations.literal: He was worshipped in the shrines of eminent officials in Henan and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was enrolled in the shrines of eminent officials in Henan and Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 子樹芝、樹萱，聖祖時，以諸生召見，令隨鵬年校書內廷。

translations.literal: His sons Shuzhi and Shuxuan, in the time of the Sacred Ancestor, were summoned as licentiates for audience and ordered to follow Pengnian in collating books within the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shuzhi and Shuxuan were summoned as licentiates during the Kangxi reign and ordered to join Chen Pengnian in collating books within the palace.

sentences.zh: 樹芝官至平越知府，樹萱官至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shuzhi rose to prefect of Pingyue; Shuxuan rose to vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhi rose to prefect of Pingyue, and Shuxuan to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 施世綸，字文賢，漢軍鑲黃旗人，瑯仲子。

translations.literal: Shi Shilun, courtesy name Wenxian, a Bannerman of the Hanjun Xianghuang Banner, second son of Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shilun, styled Wenxian, belonged to the Han Chinese Bordered Yellow Banner and was the second son of Shi Lang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年，以廕生授江南泰州知州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi, through yinsheng appointment he was made magistrate of Taizhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi he received the Taizhou magistracy in Jiangnan through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 世綸廉惠勤民，州大治。

translations.literal: Shilun was clean, kind, and diligent for the people; the prefecture was greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shilun governed with integrity, kindness, and diligence, and the prefecture flourished.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，淮安被水，上遣使督堤工，從者數十輩，驛騷擾民，世綸白其不法者治之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Huai'an suffered flooding; the emperor sent envoys to supervise dike works; several tens of attendants disturbed the people at relay stations; Shilun reported those acting unlawfully for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Huai'an was inundated; the emperor sent envoys to supervise the dikes, and their dozens of attendants harassed the people at relay stations until Shi Shilun reported the offenders for punishment.

sentences.zh: 湖北兵變，官兵赴援出州境，世綸具芻糧，而使吏人執梃列而待，兵有擾民，立捕治，兵皆斂手去。

translations.literal: When Hubei troops mutinied, officers and soldiers went to aid and crossed the prefecture border; Shilun prepared fodder and grain and had clerks and people hold clubs in ranks to wait; when soldiers disturbed the people they were immediately seized and punished, and all the troops withdrew with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: When troops mutinied in Hubei and relief forces passed through his jurisdiction, Shi Shilun supplied fodder and grain and lined clerks and townsfolk with clubs at the ready; any soldier who harassed the people was seized at once, and the troops all withdrew meekly.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，以承修京口沙船遲誤，部議降調。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, for delay in undertaking repair of Jingkou sand ships, the ministry deliberated demotion and transfer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was recommended for demotion for delays in repairing the sand boats at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 總督傅臘塔疏陳世綸清廉公直，上允留任。

translations.literal: Governor-general Fu Lata memorialized that Shilun was clean, upright, and fair; the emperor approved keeping him in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Fu Lata memorialized that Shi Shilun was incorruptible and upright, and the emperor approved his retention.

sentences.zh: 擢揚州知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 揚州民好遊蕩，世綸力禁之，俗為變。

translations.literal: The people of Yangzhou were fond of roaming dissipation; Shilun vigorously forbade it and customs were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yangzhou were prone to idle roaming; Shi Shilun strictly forbade it and changed local customs.

sentences.zh: 三十年八月，海潮驟漲，泰州范公堤圮，世綸請捐修。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirtieth year the sea tide rose sharply, the Fan Gong Dike of Taizhou collapsed, and Shilun requested donation-funded repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirtieth year a sudden tidal surge destroyed Taizhou's Fan Gong Dike, and Shi Shilun petitioned for charitable repair.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，移江寧知府。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was transferred to prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was transferred to prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，瑯卒，總督范成勳疏以世綸輿情愛戴，請在任守制；

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Lang died; Governor-general Fan Chengmo memorialized that the people's feelings loved and revered Shilun and requested mourning rites while remaining in office;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year Shi Lang died; Governor-general Fan Chengmo memorialized that the people deeply loved Shi Shilun and asked that he be allowed to observe mourning in office;

sentences.zh: 御史胡德邁疏論，世綸乃得去官，复居母喪。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Demai memorialized in dissent; only then did Shilun obtain leave from office and again observe mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Demai objected in a memorial, and only then was Shi Shilun allowed to leave office and resume mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授蘇州知府，仍請終制，辭不赴。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed prefect of Suzhou; he still requested to complete mourning and declined to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was appointed prefect of Suzhou, but he again asked to complete his mourning period and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，既終制，授江南淮徐道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, mourning having ended, he was made intendant of Huai-Xu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, when mourning was complete, he was made intendant of the Huai-Xu circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 四十年，湖南按察使員缺，九卿舉世綸，大學士伊桑阿入奏，聖祖諭曰：「朕深知世綸廉，但遇事偏執，民與諸生訟，彼必袒民；

translations.literal: In the fortieth year the Hunan surveillance commissioner post was vacant; the Nine Ministers recommended Shilun; Grand Secretary Yisang'a entered to report; the Sacred Ancestor instructed: "I deeply know Shilun's integrity, but in handling affairs he is partial and obstinate: when commoners and licentiates sue, he inevitably sides with the commoners;
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year the Hunan surveillance commission fell vacant; the Nine Ministers recommended Shi Shilun; Grand Secretary Yisang'a reported to the throne, and the Kangxi Emperor said, "I know well that Shi Shilun is incorruptible, but he is obstinate in judgment: when commoners sue licentiates, he always favors the commoners;

sentences.zh: 諸生與搢紳訟，彼必袒諸生。

translations.literal: When licentiates and gentry and officials sue, he inevitably sides with the licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: When licentiates sue officials and gentry, he always favors the licentiates.

sentences.zh: 處事惟求得中，豈偏執？

translations.literal: In handling affairs one only seeks what is central—is that partiality and obstinacy?
translations.idiomatic: In handling cases one only seeks the middle course—how is that obstinacy?

sentences.zh: 如世綸者，委以錢穀之事，則相宜耳。」

translations.literal: One such as Shilun, if entrusted with fiscal matters, would be appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: For someone like Shi Shilun, fiscal and grain affairs would suit him better.

sentences.zh: 是歲授湖南布政使。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Hunan provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Hunan administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 湖南田賦丁銀有徭費，漕米有京費。

translations.literal: In Hunan land tax and ding silver had corvée fees; tribute grain had capital fees.
translations.idiomatic: In Hunan land taxes and poll levies carried corvée surcharges, and tribute grain carried capital surcharges.

sentences.zh: 世綸至，盡革徭費，減京費四之一，民立石頌之。

translations.literal: When Shilun arrived he entirely abolished corvée fees and reduced capital fees by one-fourth; the people erected a stone to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Shilun took office he abolished the corvée surcharges entirely and cut capital surcharges by a quarter; the people erected a stone to praise him.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，移安徽布政使。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was transferred to Anhui provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was transferred to Anhui administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，遷太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was transferred to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he was made minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，坐湖南任內失察營兵掠當舖，罷職。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, because while in Hunan he failed to detect camp soldiers plundering pawnshops, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was dismissed for failing while in Hunan to prevent garrison troops from looting pawnshops.

sentences.zh: 三月，授順天府府尹，疏請禁司坊擅理詞訟、奸徒包攬捐納、牙行霸占貨物、流娼歌舞飲宴，飭部議，定為令。

translations.literal: In the third month he was appointed metropolitan prefect of Shuntian; he memorialized to forbid wards from handling lawsuits on their own, villains from monopolizing contributions and purchases, broker houses from seizing goods, and courtesans from song, dance, drink, and feasting; the ministry was ordered to deliberate and these were fixed as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was appointed Shuntian metropolitan prefect and memorialized to forbid neighborhood wards from hearing lawsuits, rascals from monopolizing contributions, brokers from seizing goods, and prostitutes from public revelry; the ministry deliberated and these became permanent regulations.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，授左副都御史，兼管府尹事。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was appointed left vice censor-in-chief, concurrently managing metropolitan prefect affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he was made left vice censor-in-chief while retaining charge of the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，遷戶部侍郎，督理錢法。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was transferred to vice minister of Revenue, supervising coinage.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was transferred to vice minister of Revenue to supervise currency.

sentences.zh: 尋調總督倉場。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to supervise the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to superintendent of the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，授雲南巡撫，未行，調漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was appointed governor of Yunnan; before departing he was transferred to governor-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was appointed governor of Yunnan, but before he could depart he was made grain-transport governor-general.

sentences.zh: 世綸察運漕積弊，革羨金，劾貪弁，除蠹役，以嚴明為治。

translations.literal: Shilun investigated accumulated abuses in transport and tribute grain, abolished surplus silver, impeached greedy officers, and removed parasitic clerks, governing with severity and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shilun exposed long-standing abuses in grain transport, abolished illicit surcharges, impeached corrupt officers, and expelled parasite clerks, governing with stern clarity.

sentences.zh: 歲督漕船，應限全完，無稍愆誤。

translations.literal: Each year he supervised tribute grain ships; within the deadline all were fully completed without the slightest delay or error.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the tribute fleets met their deadlines in full, without the slightest delay.

sentences.zh: 時西陲用兵，轉輸餽運，自河南達陝西。

translations.literal: At the time the western borders were at war; transport of provisions ran from Henan to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The western campaigns were then underway, and supplies moved from Henan to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 陝西旱飢，五十九年，上命世綸詣陝西佐總督鄂海督軍餉，並令道中勘河南府至西安黃河輓運路徑，並察陝西現存穀石數目陳奏。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered drought and famine; in the fifty-ninth year the emperor ordered Shilun to proceed to Shaanxi to assist Governor-general E Hai in supervising military provisions, and also ordered him on the route to survey the Yellow River towing transport paths from Henan prefecture to Xi'an, and inspect and report the number of grain and stone measures presently stored in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was stricken by drought and famine; in the fifty-ninth year the emperor ordered Shi Shilun to Shaanxi to assist Governor-general E Hai in provisioning the armies, to survey Yellow River transport routes from Henan prefecture to Xi'an along the way, and to report the grain stores on hand in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 世綸乃溯河西上，疏言：「河南府孟津縣至陝西太陽渡，大小數十餘灘，纖道高低不等，或在河南，或在河北。

translations.literal: Shilun then went upriver along the west bank and memorialized: "From Mengjin county in Henan prefecture to Taiyang Ford in Shaanxi there are more than several tens of large and small rapids; towing paths are uneven in height, sometimes on the Henan side, sometimes on the Hebei side.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shilun then surveyed up the west bank and reported: "From Mengjin in Henan prefecture to Taiyang Ford in Shaanxi there are dozens of rapids of varying size; towing paths rise and fall unevenly, sometimes on the south bank and sometimes on the north.

sentences.zh: 澠池以下，舟下水可載糧三百餘石，上水載及其半；

translations.literal: Below Mianchi, boats going downstream could carry more than three hundred shi of grain; going upstream they carried half that much;
translations.idiomatic: Below Mianchi, downstream boats can carry over three hundred shi of grain, and upstream about half as much;

sentences.zh: 澠池以上，河流高迅，僅可數十石。

translations.literal: Above Mianchi the river runs high and swift and can bear only several tens of shi.
translations.idiomatic: Above Mianchi the river runs swift and high, and boats carry only a few dozen shi.

sentences.zh: 自砥柱至神門無纖道，惟路旁石往往有方眼，又有石鼻，從前輓運，其跡猶存。

translations.literal: From Dizhu to Shenmen there is no towing path; only beside the road stones often have square holes, and there are also stone noses; traces of former towing transport still remain.
translations.idiomatic: From Dizhu to Shenmen there is no towing path; only stones along the road, often with square holes and stone pegs, still bear traces of the old hauling routes.

sentences.zh: 自陝州至西安府，河水平穩，俱有輓運路徑。

translations.literal: From Shaanzhou to Xi'an prefecture the river is calm and level, and all have towing transport paths.
translations.idiomatic: From Shaanzhou to Xi'an the river is calm, and hauling routes exist throughout.

sentences.zh: 謹繪圖以聞。」

translations.literal: I respectfully draw maps to report."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit maps thereof.

sentences.zh: 又言：「河南府至陝州三門，今乃無舟。

translations.literal: He also said: "From Henan prefecture to the Three Gates at Shaanzhou, now there are no boats.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported: "From Henan prefecture to the Three Gates at Shaanzhou there are presently no boats at all.

sentences.zh: 請自太陽渡以下改車運，太陽渡至西安府黨家馬頭舟行為便。

translations.literal: I request that below Taiyang Ford transport be changed to carts; from Taiyang Ford to Dangjia Matou in Xi'an prefecture boat travel is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that transport below Taiyang Ford use carts, and that from Taiyang Ford to Dangjia Matou in Xi'an prefecture boats be used.

sentences.zh: 黨家馬頭入倉復改車運，穀二十萬石都銀十萬三千兩有奇。

translations.literal: From Dangjia Matou entry to the granary, again change to cart transport; two hundred thousand shi of grain would altogether cost a little more than one hundred and three thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: From Dangjia Matou to the granaries carts should again be used; moving two hundred thousand shi of grain would cost a little over one hundred and three thousand taels of silver in all.

sentences.zh: 但運穀二十萬，止得米十萬。

translations.literal: But transporting two hundred thousand shi of grain yields only one hundred thousand shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet transporting two hundred thousand shi of grain yields only one hundred thousand shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 請令河南以二穀易一米，則運價可省其半。

translations.literal: I request ordering Henan to exchange two measures of grain for one of rice; then transport costs could be halved.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Henan exchange two shi of grain for one shi of rice, which would halve the transport costs.

sentences.zh: 若慮米難久貯，請照例出陳易新。」

translations.literal: If one fears rice cannot be stored long, I request following precedent to issue old grain and exchange for new."
translations.idiomatic: If long storage is feared, the usual practice of releasing old grain and replenishing with new may be followed.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上念陝西災，發帑金五十萬，並令酌發常平倉穀；

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, remembering Shaanxi's disaster, the emperor issued five hundred thousand taels from the treasury and also ordered discretionary release of grain from ever-normal granaries;
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor, mindful of Shaanxi's disaster, released five hundred thousand taels from the treasury and ordered discretionary release from ever-normal granaries;

sentences.zh: 又以地方官吏大半在軍前，令選部院司官詣陝西，命世綸總其事。

translations.literal: And because most local officials and clerks were at the army front, he ordered selection of ministry and court officials to proceed to Shaanxi and commanded Shilun to oversee the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: And because most local officials were at the front, he ordered ministry and court officials chosen for Shaanxi and put Shi Shilun in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 世綸令分十二路察貧民，按口分給，遠近皆遍。

translations.literal: Shilun ordered twelve routes to inspect the poor and distribute according to mouths; near and far were all covered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shilun sent twelve teams to survey the poor and distribute rations per capita until relief reached every district, near and far.

sentences.zh: 六十年春，得雨，災漸澹。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixtieth year rain fell and the disaster gradually abated.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixtieth year rain came and the famine eased.

sentences.zh: 上命世綸還理漕事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shilun to return and manage grain transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Shi Shilun back to his grain-transport duties.

sentences.zh: 六十一年四月，以病乞休，溫旨慰留，令其子廷祥馳驛省視。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixty-first year he requested retirement on grounds of illness; a warm edict comforted him and urged him to stay, ordering his son Tingxiang to ride relay horses swiftly to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixty-first year he asked to retire for illness; a warm edict urged him to remain and sent his son Tingxiang post-haste to visit him.

sentences.zh: 五月，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he died.

sentences.zh: 遺疏請隨父瑯葬福建，上允之，詔獎其清慎勤勞，予祭葬。

translations.literal: In his dying memorial he asked to be buried in Fujian following his father Lang; the emperor approved, and an edict praised his purity, caution, diligence, and labor and granted sacrificial rites and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial asked to be buried in Fujian beside his father Shi Lang; the emperor consented, praised his integrity, caution, diligence, and toil, and granted state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 世綸當官聰強果決，摧抑豪猾，禁戢胥吏。

translations.literal: Shilun in office was sharp, forceful, and resolute, crushed powerful rascals, and restrained clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In office Shi Shilun was sharp and resolute, crushed local bullies, and kept clerks in check.

sentences.zh: 所至有惠政，民號曰「青天」。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he had benevolent government; the people styled him "Blue Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he brought real benefit, and the people called him "Blue Heaven."

sentences.zh: 在江寧以憂歸，民乞留者逾萬。

translations.literal: When he left Jiangning for mourning, those begging him to stay exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When he left Jiangning for mourning, more than ten thousand people pleaded that he stay.

sentences.zh: 既不得請，人出一錢建兩亭府署前，號一文亭。

translations.literal: When the request was not granted, each person gave one cash to build two pavilions before the prefectural yamen, called the One-Cash Pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: When he could not be persuaded to stay, the people each gave a cash to erect two pavilions before the yamen, called the One-Cash Pavilions.

sentences.zh: 官府尹，步軍統領託合齊方貴幸，出必擁騶從。

translations.literal: When he was metropolitan prefect, the infantry commander Tuheqi was then in imperial favor; whenever he went out he was sure to be surrounded by mounted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan prefect he encountered the infantry commander Tuheqi, then a court favorite who never went abroad without a throng of mounted attendants.

sentences.zh: 世綸與相值，拱立道旁俟。

translations.literal: Shilun met him by chance, bowed with folded hands, and stood by the road waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When their paths crossed, Shi Shilun bowed with folded hands and stood by the road to wait.

sentences.zh: 託合齊下輿驚問，世綸抗聲曰：「國製，諸王始具騶從。

translations.literal: Tuheqi descended from his carriage in alarm and asked; Shilun spoke up loudly: "By national regulation, only princes may have mounted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Tuheqi stepped down in alarm and asked why; Shi Shilun declared loudly, "By imperial statute only princes may travel with mounted attendants.

sentences.zh: 吾以為諸王至，拱立以俟，不意為汝也！」

translations.literal: I thought princes had arrived and bowed with folded hands to wait—I did not expect it was you!"
translations.idiomatic: I thought a prince was coming and stood bowing to wait—I never imagined it was you!"

sentences.zh: 將疏劾，託合齊謝之乃已。

translations.literal: He was about to memorialize in impeachment; Tuheqi apologized and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to impeach him in a memorial, but Tuheqi apologized and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 賑陝西，陝西積儲多虛耗，將疏劾。

translations.literal: Relieving Shaanxi, he found stored grain there much depleted in false entries; he was about to memorialize in impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: While relieving Shaanxi he found the reserves largely hollowed by waste and was about to impeach those responsible.

sentences.zh: 鄂海以廷祥知會寧，語微及之，世綸曰：「吾自入官，身且不顧，何有於子？」

translations.literal: E Hai, because Tingxiang was magistrate of Huining, spoke obliquely on the matter; Shilun said: "Since I entered office I do not consider my own person—what of a son?"
translations.idiomatic: E Hai, whose son Tingxiang governed Huining, hinted at the matter; Shi Shilun said, "Since I entered office I have not spared myself—why should I spare my son?"

sentences.zh: 卒疏言之。

translations.literal: In the end he memorialized and stated it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in the end all the same.

sentences.zh: 鄂海坐罷去。

translations.literal: E Hai was consequently dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: E Hai was dismissed from office as a result.

sentences.zh: 論曰：-{于}-成龍秉剛正之性，苦節自厲，始終不渝，所至民懷其德。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Yu Chenglong bore a nature of firm uprightness, practiced harsh self-discipline and self-exertion, never changed from first to last, and wherever he went the people cherished his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Yu Chenglong had a stern upright nature, disciplined himself through hardship, and never wavered; wherever he served the people cherished him.

sentences.zh: 彭鵬拒偽命，立身不苟，在官亦以正直稱。

translations.literal: Peng Peng refused a false commission, established himself without laxity, and in office was also known for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng refused a rebel commission and lived without compromise; in office too he was famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 陳瑸起自海濱，一介不取，行能踐言。

translations.literal: Chen Bin rose from the seashore, took not even one item, and in conduct could fulfill his words.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bin rose from the coast, took nothing that was not his, and matched deed to word.

sentences.zh: 陳鵬年、施世綸明愛人，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian and Shi Shilun were bright in loving people and did not fear the strong and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian and Shi Shilun were clear-sighted in caring for the people and fearless before the powerful.

sentences.zh: 之五人者，皆自牧令起，以清節聞於時。

translations.literal: These five men all rose from magistrate and prefect posts and were known to their age for clean integrity.
translations.idiomatic: All five rose from county and prefectural posts and were famed in their day for incorruptibility.

sentences.zh: 成龍、世綸名尤盛，閭巷誦其績，久而弗渝。

translations.literal: Chenglong and Shilun were especially celebrated in reputation; lanes and alleys recited their achievements, long enduring without change.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong and Shi Shilun were the most renowned; common folk recited their deeds for generations without forgetting.

sentences.zh: 康熙間吏治清明，廉吏接踵起，聖祖所以保全諸臣，其效大矣。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period official governance was clear and bright, honest officials rose in succession, and the means by which the Sacred Ancestor preserved these ministers—their effect was great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi officialdom was unusually clear, and honest officials arose one after another; the Kangxi Emperor's way of protecting such men yielded vast effects indeed.
